34	
35	## Player Fantasy
36	
37	**The fantasy in one sentence.** *"The light we need to keep the ship alive is the light that brings it, and we survive by reading the dark it walks through, never by fighting it."* This is not a scary-monster fantasy. It is a **prey-with-knowledge** fantasy that grows out of two locked facts that collide on purpose: every channelled repair verb is lit-only (Interaction `NOT_LIT`, IA-6) and the chest lamp is hands-free (user decision), so to fix the scrubber you must be lit; and the horror's one preference among living seats is the highest `lux_pm`, recomputed from physical light on every run with no stored value (HE-13). The core Horror decision of every BREACH is therefore the game's core fantasy compressed: *keep the ship breathing (light on, channel the repair) or keep the body breathing (lamp off, close a door, step out of the reach, pod-hop).* The Core Fantasy line "the ship is alive because we keep it alive, minute by minute" becomes literal: **the minute you spend keeping it alive is a minute you are visible.**
38	
39	**Framing (orchestrator ruling: creative-director framing A, with B as tonal layer).** Direct framing, **"Read the Dark"**: *it comes to the light; I read its trail and choose when to be seen.* Every rule in this document can be checked against that sentence, it puts the player's competence in reading rather than in reflexes, and it turns the lit-only repair rule into the central dilemma instead of a friction. Framing **B, "The Web's Hand"** (the horror is the web reaching into the ship through this limb because the crew has earned its attention) is adopted as the fiction behind A only: it justifies why the thing is "of the web" and why it casts no shadow (see the fiction gloss below). Framing **C, "The Hunter"** (something is tracking us) is rejected: a hunter remembers, which requires a stored pursuit or last-seen value, which is a hidden aggro number and fails Pillar 1's own design test. *(Framing A with B as fiction, and the rejection of C, were ratified without change at the CD-GDD-ALIGN gate; later edits must not drift from "the minute you spend keeping it alive is a minute you are visible".)*
40	
41	**The anchor moment: a limb entering the cone before the body.** The player is crouched at a derelict's failing scrubber, channel bar half full, chest lamp lit because the verb demands it. At the edge of the cone, something thin and segmented arrives first: one long jointed limb, iridescent only where the beam touches it, laid along the floor toward them. The body is still in the dark. The player has a choice that is legible, not a reflex test: finish the channel (the bar shows the ticks left) or abandon it and walk out of the reach. If they walk, nothing touches them; the scrubber is still broken. The feeling is *I lived, and the ship paid.*
42	
43	| Tick (from TELL entry) | Attention (owned there, read-only here) | Horror (this GDD) | What the player can perceive |
44	|---|---|---|---|
45	| T = 0 | TELL begins; `tell_epoch` +1; locus recorded (AT-14) | The entity leaves LURK; if the locus body is not its body it leaves through the hull (egress mark) and enters `TRANSIT`, even when its own body is unloaded (HE-20) | Attention's global tell (beat on every lit region, filaments, dust turning): "it noticed" |
46	| T >= `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS` − `INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS` (mark), `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS` (body) (240 / 300 [PH]) | TELL continues | Ingress through a hull segment one room hop from the brightest living seat's room, never into a seat's room, never inside `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` (HE-20) | The first local sign: a radial hairline on a hull face, rime branching from it, a fixture nearby dipping on its own rhythm |
47	| `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS` to tell end | The tell length was drawn in [`TELL_DRAW_LO`, `TELL_DRAW_HI`], never below `TELL_MIN_TICKS` | STALK at `V_CREEP_MPX`; never within `LURK_STANDOFF_PX`; no RUPTURE, no GOUGE, no harm (HE-12) | A visible stalk of at least `TELL_MIN_TICKS − INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS` = 300 ticks at the placeholders, typically 600 to 1500 |
48	| BREACH entry | `exogenous_permitted(section)` true in `locus_body` | Approach at `V_HUNT_MPX` toward the highest-`lux_pm` living seat | "Controlled panic, more things moving, not the screen fighting the player" (ART 2.8) |
49	| REACH start | n/a | The strike point is LOCKED (non-tracking); `UNFOLD_TICKS` drawn in [`UNFOLD_LO`, `UNFOLD_HI`] = [95, 180] ticks [PH] (HE-14, HE-F5) | **The limb enters the cone.** About 1.6 to 3 seconds of unfold, then a held stillness |
50	| REACH end | The predicate is re-checked | STRIKE resolves only if `exogenous_permitted` still holds; every living seat in the disc takes `STRIKE_BP` (HE-15) | A snap, the touch-down smear and Audio's positional strike cue. Strike one is witnessed by the strike itself, by Suit's integrity reading (the STRAINED rung is inert and carries no witness, by Suit's design) and, if a seat was hit, by the STRUCK hairline burst laid at P that a miss never leaves; the first physical consequence is strike two (leak, seam jet, CRITICAL, stagger, walk-only) |
51	
52	**Worked moment (single player, derelict B, placeholders).** The player is at 40 % of a scrubber channel with the lamp on; `lux_pm` reads 1000 because the owner stands in their own light (EM-21). A TELL begins at T = 0 with a drawn length of 1200. Ingress is at T = 300, one room away; the hairline and rime are visible through the doorway; the body crosses the door frame near T = 700. BREACH begins at T = 1200 and the horror closes at `V_HUNT_MPX` 1500 (1.5 px per tick). It closes from the standoff (192 px) to `REACH_RANGE_PX` (96 px) in 64 ticks, so its REACH starts on the run grid at T = 1265; `UNFOLD_TICKS` draws 135. The player sees the limb at T = 1265, abandons the channel at T = 1319 (54 ticks of reaction, `REACT_ALLOW_TICKS_HORROR`) and walks at `V_WALK` 2: 72 px in 36 ticks on a cardinal octant, so (with the kernel's one-tick command application, KRN D.4: the command issued at T = 1319 first moves them in tick 1320, and the 36th step lands in tick 1355) they stand outside the disc at T = 1355, 45 ticks before the snap at T = 1400 (T = 1356 and 44 ticks on a diagonal octant) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: recomputed under HE-F5's tick-indexing convention, G4)*. No harm. One wet smear sits where the tip rested; if the tip was within `HULL_CONTACT_PX` of a hull face, radial hairlines and a hull GOUGE mark the wall. The scrubber is still broken.
53	
54	**Explicitly not a tell length.** The kernel's illustrative `rng_int(600, 1800)` on the stream name `"horror.tell"` (KRN D.10) is an example, not Horror's tell and not Horror's REACH range. The Pillar 2 requirement of 10 to 30 seconds (LSG:144) is met by Attention's window (AT-15); Horror's stalk and REACH are **additive layers and never a substitute**, and nothing in this GDD shortens Attention's tell (HE-9). The stream `"attention.tell"` is Attention's.
55	
56	**Pillar text served (verbatim) and the design tests as they bite Horror.**
57	
58	| Pillar | Text (game-concept) | How this GDD serves it |
59	|---|---|---|
60	| **P2 Dread Before Chaos** (primary) | "Every breach is preceded by a tell a careful player could have perceived (sound, light, gauge drift, hull stress)." Design test: *breach fires at a hidden threshold vs. breach preceded by a 10-30 second escalating tell -> the tell.* | Every lethal act lands inside Attention's told breach (AT-15) and is further preceded by the visible stalk and by the REACH telegraph at a locked point. Three told layers, never one. |
61	| **P1 The World Never Lies** (primary) | "Pipes leak, frost forms, air hisses; the physical world is ground truth." Design test: *a hidden stat vs. a visibly leaking pipe -> the pipe.* | The horror is a SIM entity at a true position that leaves true marks, true Graph footprints and true light disturbance. No aggro or threat number exists, stored or derived. |
62	| **P3 The Web Watches** (serves) | "Attention is shown in the world (creaking, flicker, filament movement), never as a hidden meter. Restraint and stealth are real strategies." | The horror is Attention's consequence, never a second meter (AT-2). Its CALM, TELL and BREACH behaviour is gated by `attention.view.phase` only; going dark is real counterplay. |
63	| **P4 Sanity Rewrites Reality** (serves) | "A hidden real entity still leaves its P1/P2 footprint (sound, frost, hull stress, light disturbance) — the hallucination hides the body, never the trail." | Horror owns the web-grammar half of that guarantee: marks, disturbance state and Graph footprints are bit-identical whether or not any viewer's body-hide is active (HE-32). |
64	| **P5 Deeper Is Richer, Loss Is Not Total** (light) | "Losing the home-ship or a crewmate costs ship and body, never knowledge." | Death by horror restores from the newest autosave (SL-7); what the player learned about reach, rime and light survives in their head and, at Vertical Slice, in the Codex through stable `type_id` and `tell_id` enumerations. |
65	
66	*Design test (this system):* **a horror that reacts to a number nobody can see vs. a horror that reacts to light the player chose to show -> the light.** *Secondary test (Pillar 2 at body scale):* **a strike that lands from the dark vs. a limb that enters the cone before the body at a point that no longer moves -> the limb.** The tests decide four recurring debates: keep a "last target" so the horror follows the player who switched the lamp off (no: turning the lamp off removes the seat from preference on the next run; memory would be a hidden number); let the strike track a moving player for "fairness of difficulty" (no: the point locks at REACH start); let it charge in CALM (no: CALM is non-lethal by construction and it never comes inside `LURK_STANDOFF_PX`); make the beam repel it, or make it shrug the beam off to stay scary (neither: the beam only reveals, EM:89 adopted verbatim).
67	
68	**How the fantasy deepens under hallucination.** The horror's truth is its trail. Because a real entity always writes marks, Graph footprints and disturbance state and a phantom never does, low sanity turns "is it there?" into "is the floor marked?". The player stops reading the body and starts reading the ship, which is exactly the Pillar 1 and 4 tension the concept calls "the game". Horror's obligations in each class are small and absolute.
69	
70	| Class | What the player is shown | The channel of truth that remains | Horror's obligation |
71	|---|---|---|---|
72	| (a) phantom entity (invented) | The Filter draws a horror rig from a phantom pose stream; it may lunge | No told breach precedes it (TellAudit records nothing, AT E-53); no rime, smear or hairline; no disturbance; no Graph footprint; the suit rung does not move | Keep `horror.view` real-only; the rig presenter accepts any pose stream (HE-40) |
73	| (a) hidden real entity (Vertical Slice) | The Filter undraws the body for one seat | Marks, disturbance, M17 writes and suit damage are bit-identical with or without the hide; a saner crewmate may still see the body | Keep every real entity registered with a true anchor; read no perception state (H5, CR-12) |
74	| (b) false system state | Gauges and sprites lie | Horror touches nothing in (b); its RUPTURE and GOUGE surface as true Graph descriptors that Failure & Trail draws (FT-31) | None |
75	| (c) crewmate as horror (Vertical Slice) | The Filter substitutes the horror rig for a crewmate's body, driven by their true velocity | The true beam: "a horror with a player's beam is your friend" (ART:292); a real horror emits nothing, so the beam stays a perfect discriminator | Real horrors never carry or emit light (HE-2) |
76	| (d) phantom salvage | Not Horror's | n/a | None |
77	
78	Three falsifiers cost the player something, as Pillar 4 demands (checking costs time, risk or trust): **look at the floor** (time: in the dark you must light it, which draws the real one), **check the phase** (risk: is Attention's tell running?), **ask the crewmate** (trust; co-op). The no-shadow rule adds a fourth, free falsifier at stage 2: *a shadow with no occluder is never the web: it is you.*
79	
80	**Fiction gloss for the no-shadow rule (creative-director; adopted at the CD-GDD-ALIGN gate; to be written into ART:542 as part of the owed refresh, which gates the rig's asset-spec).** *"The web does not stop light; it only takes it."* Web-matter is real: it stands on the deck, scars the hull, leaves rime where it passed and moves dust. But light goes through it as through a filament: the beam shows its surface as a thin iridescent band and continues to whatever is behind it. Nothing that belongs to the web casts a shadow, so a shadow with no occluder is never the web.
81	
82	**Reference techniques, adopt and reject.**
83	
84	| Reference | Technique | Verdict | Where it lands |
85	|---|---|---|---|
86	| *Alien: Isolation* | One persistent, physically present entity, never despawned | ADOPT | HE-1, HE-20 |
87	| *Alien: Isolation* | A director's "menace gauge" steering the alien | REJECT: guard rail 1 (no threat value); Attention is the only director (AT-2) | HE-7 |
88	| *Alien: Isolation* | Grab-instakill on contact | REJECT: three told strikes | HE-15 |
89	| *Amnesia: The Dark Descent* | "You cannot fight it, only hide" | ADOPT in spirit | HE-38 |
90	| *Amnesia* | Sanity drains from looking at the monster | REJECT here: Sanity owns exposure; Horror computes none | HE-40 |
91	| *Amnesia* | The monster vanishes when out of sight | REJECT: a SIM entity at a true position; dormancy freezes, never despawns | HE-21 |
92	| *Darkwood* | Light attracts; the world carries marks of what passed | ADOPT | HE-13, HE-27 |
93	| *Darkwood* | Melee combat, crafted weapons | REJECT: anti-pillar; HORROR takes no verb | HE-38 |
94	| *Barotrauma* | Creatures that hole the hull; crew patch it | ADOPT | HE-16 |
95	| *Barotrauma* | Turrets, weapons, creature loot | REJECT | HE-38 |
96	| *Project Zomboid* | Death is final and common ("it happens") | ADOPT (user decision) | HE-15 |
97	| *Project Zomboid* | A killable horde as content | REJECT: "horrors are avoided and survived, not farmed" | HE-38 |
98	| *Pandorum* (film) | A hands-free chest lamp in a dark derelict; hunters in the margins of the light | ADOPT (user decision) | HE-13 |
99	| *Pandorum* | Fighting the hunters hand to hand | REJECT: no attack input (PC-12) | HE-38 |
100	| *Beyond the Aquila Rift* | The kindness of the lie: the wrongness is in what you are shown | ADOPT, routed to Sanity and the Filter | HE-32 |
101	| *Annihilation* (film) | The shimmer: iridescence as the signature of something not of our world | ADOPT: a band only under light, never a fill | Visual/Audio Requirements |
102	| *The Thing* | The body as wrongness, imitation of crew | REJECT for Horror: class (c) is a render substitution owned by the Filter | HE-40 |
103	| Souls-like games | A long, readable wind-up at a fixed point | ADOPT | HE-14 |
104	| Action games | Hit-stop, screen shake, damage numbers | REJECT: the camera refuses horror callers (PIPE C1, C9) | HE-38 |
105	
106	**Tone and vocabulary.** Patient, physical, quiet; closer to weather with intent than to a monster with a personality. It never roars at the camera, never poses, never "spots" anyone; it arrives in increments the player could have seen. Used in this document and in any player-facing text: reach, unfold, snap, strike, lurk, stalk, retreat, ingress, egress, "it noticed" (Attention's mood), "it comes to the light", smear, branching rime, radial hairline, "the trail", "the floor remembers", dip (for a lamp). Never used, outside a quotation or a negation: `threat`, `aggro`, `alert`, `awareness`, `suspicion`, `hate`, `detect` as horror state; `enemy`, `mob`, `boss`, `spawn` (use ingress), `kill`, `damage` (use `strike_bp`); `flicker` of a fixture (use dip); `meter`, `bar`, `gauge`, `indicator` near a horror or proximity; `real occlusion`, `cast shadow`, `occlude the beam`. These double as the stale-token lint (Acceptance Criteria).
107	
108	**Emotional arc across a breach cycle (mapped to Attention's phases).**
109	
110	| Phase | Intended emotion | Horror's contribution | Flow note |
111	|---|---|---|---|
112	| CALM | Unease, then orientation: "it lives in this body, and its trail is fresh" (information, never danger: CALM is non-lethal by construction, HE-11) | LURK: may be seen at a distance and cannot harm; marks age; disturbance dips near it | Flow of work with a background tax of glances at the floor, paid in choices (route, lamp, which job first), not in fear of a hit |
113	| TELL | Dread, rising | STALK visible; ingress hairline and rime; disturbance near it | An intentional flow break: the player reprioritises |
114	| BREACH | Controlled panic | Approach, REACH telegraph, STRIKE at a locked point | Choice under time, never a reflex test (the walk-out bound) |
115	| SUBSIDING | Relief with residue | RETREAT; no new REACH starts | Recovery |
116	| After | Reading the aftermath | Marks: where it came from, where it touched the hull | Discovery: "it came in through there" |
117	
118	**Anti-pillar guard rails (restated as lints in Acceptance Criteria).**
119	1. **Not a combat game.** No horror HP, no kill state, no loot, no XP, no kill counter, no hit feedback for tool use, no player damage output; HORROR subjects take no verb at MVP (`INVALID_TARGET`, IA-39); the beam only reveals.
120	2. **No reward path.** Nothing drops, nothing unlocks, no codex entry is earned by approaching a horror at MVP. Surviving costs the ship (footprints), never pays.
121	3. **Not intentional PvP.** A horror's lethal act on a crew body is inside the told breach and audited by TellAudit (AT-15 R15); friendly harm stays Interaction plus Sanity; Horror never routes harm between players.
122	4. **Not a freeform builder, no authored story.** Horror places nothing and narrates nothing; Derelict Authoring "places no entity" (DA:101); ingress is derived from Attention's locus and Emitter reads, never a trigger volume ("monster closets: REJECT").
123	5. **No win state.** The horror cannot be removed from the world; it only retreats.
124	6. **Death is lethal (user), and is not Horror's.** Horror owns the act and its tells; DOWNED and DEAD are Suit's (SE-24); restore from the newest autosave is Save/Load's (SL-7). No death screen, no beat.
125	
126	**Validation targets (creative-director, `[PLACEHOLDER]`, measured in MVP playtests of the concept's 30-minute solo session).** (1) *Fair death:* at least 80 % of horror-caused deaths are described unprompted, or on one neutral question, with a cause the player saw ("I saw the arm", "I stayed in the light too long"); below 60 % the telegraph or stalk is failing. (2) *Not an alarm monster:* in at least 70 % of sessions the player sees the horror or its fresh marks during CALM at least once. (3) *The dilemma exists:* at least half of playtesters, asked "what did you do when it came?", describe turning the lamp off, abandoning a repair or closing a door; if the dominant answer is "I ran", target preference by light is not legible. (4) *No hidden-number belief:* zero playtesters describe the horror "remembering" or "locking on" across a lamp-off. (5) *Marks read as web, not ship:* a blind classification of rime against coolant frost is correct at least 90 % at k = 1, `k_auto` and `k_auto + 2`. (6) *Teeth:* in a replay of a breach on a clean ship, the player loses at least one repair's worth of progress or one suit rung in at least 60 % of breaches they choose to commit through lit. (7) *A CALM sighting changes behaviour:* at least 60 % of testers who saw the horror or a fresh mark in CALM report, unprompted or on one neutral question ("did seeing it change what you did next?"), that it changed what they did (the route, the lamp, or which job they took first). If this fails, the first lever is `RETURN_HOME` 0 (OQ-1); HE-11 is not relaxed, because CALM stays non-lethal to protect Pillar 2.
127

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

</system-reminder>

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

</system-reminder>

130	### Core Rules
131	
132	Rule ids are `HE-n`; formulas `HE-F n` (Formulas section, ids reserved in the index at the end of this section); edge cases `E-HE-n`; acceptance criteria `AC-HE-n`; conflicts `C-HE-n`. Every Horror-owned number is `[PLACEHOLDER]` and a registry candidate unless marked CITED (a locked name quoted verbatim with its registry value) or DERIVED. The Graph's `RUPTURE_HP`, `BREACH_HP`, `FOOTPRINT_MAX_Q`, `FOOTPRINT_MAX_GOUGE_BP`, `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS` and `C_TILE` are Life-Support Graph registry constants (registered 2026-10-27), cited with the registry value and their LSG line and never restated as Horror's own. Rules state observable behaviour and contracts; implementation patterns are marked "-> ADR candidate". "Run" means one execution of the `horror.step` hook (every 5th tick).
133	
134	#### Group A — Identity, scope and ownership
135	
136	**HE-1. One type, one instance, one behaviour cycle.** *Rule.* MVP ships exactly one type row, `horror_t01` (a placeholder name, renamed never aliased: floor-attached, three-branch, about 1.5 times crewmate height, one extensible reach limb; the art bible's outer-ring working target, ART:546), at most `HORROR_MAX_MVP` 1 resident record, and one behaviour cycle: **LURK (CALM) / STALK (TELL) → REACH (telegraph) → STRIKE → RETREAT**, plus `TRANSIT` while it passes through a hull. The motion vocabulary of the art matrix maps onto it as *creep* (LURK, STALK, RETREAT), *unfold* (REACH) and *snap* (STRIKE). "One behaviour" is **one cycle of one type, never three monsters.** More types, per-ring rosters, filament-riders, hidden-entity wiring, `repel`, flares and decoys, and co-op replication are Vertical Slice and are named in Open Questions and in the block shape only. *Why.* The concept's MVP item 4 is "Attention with one threshold and one horror behaviour"; AT-11 makes a told breach without teeth a named design failure (cry-wolf; commit dominates abort), and the art bible names the reach as the signature image (ART 5.4). *Cites.* AT:197, AT:373, CON MVP definition, ART:546.
137	
138	**HE-2. A real horror is a true SIM entity that touches nothing optical.** *Rule.* A horror has a true integer position in its own block, is solid to Layout solids and to nothing else (it passes through crewmates and they through it, BDY-17), is drawn in the single Y-sorted layer so its sprite hides what stands behind it, is hidden by walls and by darkness, and is revealed only by light. It **contributes no occluder, casts no shadow, emits nothing, and never changes the beam, any subject's `lux`, `lit` or any emitter field.** "Real occlusion" in the index row and the routed thread is read as *visual opacity by draw order plus locomotion against Layout solids*, never as a `LightOccluder2D`. Nothing a horror does is a light event except the disturbance state of HE-35, which Lighting reads and executes. *Why.* Three designed GDDs decide it (EM-20 (c) and AC-24; Lighting rail 10 "Horrors cast no shadow and emit nothing" and AC-LO-16; Failure & Trail FT-31) and the art bible's own recommendation agrees (ART:296); a horror shadow would destroy the free stage-2 sanity falsifier "a shadow with no occluder" and with it Pillar 4's "no lie is unfalsifiable". "Displace dust" from the art bible is retained in spirit through the marks of HE-30, not through the Attention Presenter's shared dust process. *(orchestrator ruling: option A, affirmed by the creative-director at the CD-GDD-ALIGN gate as R1; the fiction gloss "the web does not stop light; it only takes it" is adopted; the wording refreshes are owed rows, never edits here.)* **Gate.** Until the owed ART:542, ART 5.5, PIPE:140 and IDX:35 refresh rows land, the art bible and this GDD contradict each other; those rows are a BLOCKING precondition of `/asset-spec` for the rig (AC-HE-123), as C-HE-21 is for rime. *Cites.* EM:208, LO:151, FT:199, ART:296, ART:542.
139	
140	**HE-3. Block and hook identity.** *Rule.* Block `horror.state`: class `SIM`, `persist` true, `persist_scope` WORLD, scope SHARED, `repl_hint` SHARED_SUMMARY, `schema_version` 1, `supported_versions` [1], `restore_after` `[layout.state, graph.state, emitter.state, attention.state]`. Hook `horror.step`: divisor 5, offset 0, `after: [attention.step, emitter.place]` (the must-repeats of Attention (AT:373), the Emitter (EM AC-60) and the kernel (KRN:201), exactly as ruled; C-HE-20 closed). A hook id that is unknown at boot fails boot (CR-3, no alias concept); grep of `horror.step`, `horror.state` and `horror.view` across the neighbours before closing found no collision. The read view is `horror.view` (HE-37). *Why.* `body.integrate` precedes `horror.step` on every Horror tick through `emitter.place`'s own `after` list (EM:104: `after: [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]`) and the CR-3 total order, so the same-tick seat read that the exact walk-out arithmetic of HE-F2 needs holds without extending the ruled list; Horror writes nothing Body reads, so no cycle can form. A one-tick-stale seat read would let an escaping seat read up to 2 px closer than it is. *Cites.* KRN:71, KRN:201, EM:104, AT:125-131, BDY-8.
141	
142	**HE-4. Cadence: one run is one rig pose, and what Horror reads between Attention's runs.** *Rule.* `horror.step` runs on ticks that are multiples of 5 (12 Hz), so one run is exactly one 12 fps rig pose (PIPE row 14). Attention and the Graph run at divisor 6; LCM(5, 6) = 30, so the two hooks coincide only when `T mod 30 = 0`, and CR-3's `after` orders the pair only on those ticks. On every other run Horror reads `attention.view` **as committed by Attention's most recent run**; this is a reading of committed state, not a new kernel rule. Presentation interpolates `pos_prev` to `pos_curr` across the five ticks of a run; the rig pose is stepped, never tweened. Every Horror duration is authored as an integer count of runs and published in ticks as `runs × 5` (`HORROR_RUN_TICKS` 5, DERIVED from the divisor); a duration that is not a multiple of 5 is a data-load lint failure (it would silently round up to the next run, a 1 to 4 tick bias that matters at the `UNFOLD_LO` bound). **The lint covers every SIM-clock duration** (`UNFOLD_LO`, `UNFOLD_HI`, `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS`, `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS`, `RETURN_DELAY_TICKS`, `LURK_DWELL_TICKS` and the rest of the type row); it **exempts the L3 disturbance lengths `L3_DUR_LO` and `L3_DUR_HI`** (18 and 30), which are published to Lighting in ticks and are presentation-timed (LO-19, the gutter grammar), not run-quantised: a disturbance *starts* on a run, its length does not round to one (C-HE-29). *Cites.* PIPE:303, KRN:71, HE-F5.
143	
144	**HE-5. Data-driven type row.** *Rule.* Every per-type value lives in a data file keyed by `type_id`; behaviour code is generic over the row and contains no behavioural constant. A row carries: `v_creep_mpx`, `v_hunt_mpx`, `r_snap_px`, `reach_range_px`, `hull_contact_px`, `strike_bp`, `strike_cooldown_ticks`, `strike_hold_runs`, `unfold_lo`, `unfold_hi`, `lurk_standoff_px`, `lurk_dwell_ticks`, the L3 constants, the mark and rig asset ids. The data lint refuses any field named `damage`, `accuracy`, `armour`, `dps`, `xp`, `unlock`, `health`, `hp`, `kill`, `loot`, `threat`, `aggro` or `hate` (Horror's own harm field is `strike_bp`, a Suit-scale amount, never `damage`). *Why.* Coding standards (gameplay values are data-driven) and the Item DB's lint AP-2; the field list is also the anti-combat guard (HE-38). *Cites.* IDB:97.
145	
146	**HE-6. Boundaries.** *Rule.* Horror does not read or write Attention's level, does not call `set_beacon`, does not schedule a breach, does not add a Graph footprint kind, does not read any `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, does not move, push or stagger a player (the stagger is the Controller's response to the Suit rung), places no content, narrates nothing, calls no physics query, owns no sound, mix or cue name, owns no HUD element, and holds no stimulus tracker, accumulator, "awareness", "alert", "threat" or "aggro" value, persisted or derived. *Why.* Guard rail 1: absorbing Attention is the most likely way this GDD drifts; the grep of this document for those words outside a negation returns zero (Acceptance Criteria lint).
147	
148	#### Group B — Permission, tell composition and the audit
149	
150	**HE-7. Phase-sourced behaviour, no stored drive.** *Rule.* Every transition between LURK and STALK, and every harm gate, is a function of `attention.view` fields only: `phase`, `tell_epoch`, `tell_outcome`, `locus_section_id`, `exogenous_permitted(section)`, `breach_enter_T`, `phase_enter_T`. The target (HE-13) is recomputed from physical `lux` on every run and is **not persisted**. The only things the record remembers are where it is, what state it is in since when, what it has already done this `tell_epoch` (counts), the locked point of a REACH in flight, and the stream counter. **Debug surface** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: a lethal AI cannot be playtested blind)*: each run also publishes a **non-persisted, non-hashed record `horror.view.debug`** on Horror's registered diagnostics channel (Debug Overlay DO-12, dev builds only), holding the current target ref or ANCHOR with each candidate's `lux_pm`, the goal room and the surrogate goal, the next hop, the transition guard that fired (1 to 7) and the HE-14 condition (a) to (f) that failed last, `hold_runs`, `blocked_runs`, `horror_wedged`, and the `linked` and `connected` results for the nearest seat *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. It is derived from the run, never read back: **no SIM rule, guard, formula or hash input may read `horror.view.debug`** (a lint, AC-HE-135), it is absent from `horror.state`, and it is never an accessibility or player surface (UI Requirements). *Why.* AT-2 (one level for the world), Pillar 1 (no hidden stat), guard rail 1. *Cites.* AT:139, AT:214-232.
151	
152	**HE-8. The permission predicate, repeated at three check points.** *Rule.* Every web-originated harm call (M17 RUPTURE, M17 GOUGE, `apply_suit_damage`) is made only if `exogenous_permitted(section)` holds **at the call tick**, where for a bodily hit `section` is Body's `actor_section(seat)` (crew-body scope, AT-15 R15; not the Graph's `section_of`) and for a hull deposit it is the section of the hull segment. The three check points are: (1) **REACH begin** (HE-14 condition c), (2) **STRIKE entry** (HE-15), (3) **every M17 RUPTURE or GOUGE call** (HE-16, HE-29). **CHILL is a non-harm footprint, permitted in any phase, bounded by HE-F4 and HE-31** (C-HE-28). A REACH may *begin* only in BREACH (not SUBSIDING); an in-flight REACH resolves only if the predicate still holds at its last tick, otherwise it fizzles with no harm, no hairlines, no GOUGE or RUPTURE (a touch-down smear already laid at the hold stage stays: it is true; a fizzle before the hold stage lays none) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Horror issues no STRESS (Attention's alone, AT-11). The registered formula `tell_window_contract` is the audit: for every harm event `e` there is an epoch `k` with `tell_start_k + tell_len_k <= t_e < subside_end_k`, `tell_len_k >= TELL_MIN_TICKS` and `section_e` in `locus_body_k` (the epoch's locus body in force at `t_e`: recorded at TELL entry, replaced only by an AT-14 fallback that TellAudit records as LOCUS_FALLBACK); zero violations over a replay. This GDD **repeats** AT-15; it does not restate a different rule. *Cites.* AT:211, REG `tell_window_contract`, AT:794-810.
153	
154	**HE-9. Tell composition: additive layers, never a substitute.** *Rule.* The Graph's 10-30 s requirement (LSG:144, LSG:1063) is met by **Attention's window** (AT-15); nothing in Horror shortens it, defers it or replaces it. Horror adds layers on top, and a harm path that skips one of them is a defect:
155	
156	| Layer | Owner | Duration | What the player can perceive | Present for |
157	|---|---|---|---|---|
158	| L0 Attention tell | Attention | `TELL_MIN_TICKS` 600 to `TELL_MAX_TICKS` 1800 | beats, filaments, dust, lamp gutter, audio (Attention's) | every harm path |
159	| L1 Presence and stalk | Horror | from ingress (at least `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS` after TELL entry) or from TELL entry if already resident, to the first REACH | the entity in light, marks, disturbance dips, audio facts | bodily and hull paths |
160	| L2 REACH telegraph | Horror | `UNFOLD_TICKS` per strike, 95 to 180 ticks | the limb entering the cone before the body, tip resting on the locked point | every strike |
161	| L3 Footprint trail | Horror | continuous, any phase | smear, rime, hairlines | all |
162	| L4 Hull "scrape" | Horror | at least `min_gap` (> `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS`, HE-F15) before a RUPTURE, because the RUPTURE needs the segment in `gouged_seg_ids` from an earlier strike *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | a GOUGE with radial hairlines on the same segment (HE-16) | RUPTURE only |
163	
164	The kernel's illustrative `rng_int(600, 1800)` on the stream name `"horror.tell"` (KRN D.10) is **not** Horror's tell length and not Horror's REACH range; the stream `"attention.tell"` is Attention's. Horror draws from `"horror.tell"` only the REACH length (HE-14). *Cites.* LSG:144, AT:211, KRN D.10, reflexion entry on examples read as contracts.
165	
166	**HE-10. TellAudit and the crew-body scope.** *Rule.* Horror publishes in `horror.view` the facts a `TellAudit` replay needs for every harm event (HE-37: `strike_T`, the seats hit, the hull segments gouged or ruptured, the `tell_epoch` it ran in) and submits no harm that the predicate would reject. A lethal act on a crew body outside a told breach is exactly the ambush Pillar 2 forbids, and Horror's stalk is additive and never a substitute. A restored CALM save never contains a lethal horror adjacent to a seat (CALM is non-lethal by construction, HE-11), so autosave needs no Horror-specific gate (SL-5 unchanged); if HE-11 is ever relaxed, SL-5 must be revisited. *Cites.* AT:211, SL:190.
167	
168	#### Group C — The behaviour cycle
169	
170	**HE-11. LURK: the non-lethal CALM presence.** *Rule.* In CALM a resident record is in LURK in its current body. It loiters at `V_CREEP_MPX` between waypoints drawn from Layout `anchor_geometry`: it dwells `LURK_DWELL_TICKS` at a waypoint, then the next waypoint is the lowest-hash candidate (`he_hash(entity_id, dwell_index, anchor_local_key, SALT_WP)`, HE-42; the chosen waypoint is held in the persisted `goal_wp` and the dwell start in `dwell_start_T`, HE-41) among waypoints in loaded sections of its body that are at least `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` from every living seat. It **never starts a move that brings it, or leaves it, nearer than `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` to a living seat** (the invariant is on the horror's own motion: a seat that walks toward it closes the gap itself, and the horror then steps away along the room graph; if cornered it holds still and does nothing). **Every `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` comparison in this rule (the standoff, the step-away and the waypoint filter) applies only to a seat for which `linked(horror, seat)` holds (HE-19)**: a room-level test that does not change while both stand in their rooms, so a horror at a doorway cannot oscillate between the standoff and step-away rules on a jamb graze, and a seat two short rooms away in open line of sight is linked; a seat in an unlinked room behind a wall does not push it away and is not a reason to hold still *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. It deposits no RUPTURE and no GOUGE and applies no suit damage; it may be seen, lays marks (HE-30), makes CHILL deposits (HE-27) and disturbance dips (HE-35). A seat may walk through it (no collision, BDY-17); that costs nothing and is a free moment of inspection. Its transitions out of LURK come **only from `attention.view.phase`**, never from the player's light, noise or distance. *Why.* Attention's "CALM is never known-safe" (AT:92, AT:373) is a claim about the phase (a TELL can begin at any time), not a claim that this presence can hurt, and this rule does not imply one: the CALM presence is provably harmless (no harm call, the standoff, the step-away) and **what a CALM sighting is worth is information**: which body it lives in (`RETURN_HOME`), and that its trail and rime are fresh (stage-0 marks), so the player may change the route, the lamp or the first job. It is not made dangerous to keep the dread up, because a harm in CALM would arrive with no tell and break Pillar 2; the standoff and the phase-only transitions also keep it from becoming a timer or a second meter (AT-2). Validation target (7) measures whether the information is used (AC-HE-122); if it is not, the first lever is `RETURN_HOME` 0 (OQ-1), never relaxing this rule. *Cites.* AT:92, AT:373.
171	
172	**HE-12. STALK: creep in a TELL, hunt in a BREACH.** *Rule.* On a TELL entry (a `tell_epoch` different from the record's `last_seen_tell_epoch`; **this comparison is the first evaluation for every record in every run, ahead of the dormancy guard**, States and Transitions guard 2) a record whose body holds the locus goes LURK → STALK; a record in another body goes LURK → TRANSIT (HE-20), **even when its own body is unloaded** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. In a TELL, STALK moves toward the target (HE-13) at `V_CREEP_MPX` and stops at `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` from every living seat that is `linked` to it (HE-19) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; it deposits no RUPTURE and no GOUGE and calls no `apply_suit_damage`. In BREACH it moves at `V_HUNT_MPX` and closes to `REACH_RANGE_PX` of the target point. STALK is one state; the speed is a function of `attention.view.phase`. **A TELL abort** (the phase leaves TELL with an aborted `tell_outcome`) returns STALK to LURK with no strike and no mark burst, and **cancels an outbound TRANSIT** (HE-20) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Entering SUBSIDING sends STALK to RETREAT. *Why.* Pillar 2 (the stalk is the additive earlier layer) and Pillar 3. *Cites.* AT:373, AT-16.

173	
174	**HE-13. Target from physical light.** *Rule.* Candidates are living seats (not DOWNED, DEAD or IN_POD per the Controller's `loco_state`) whose `actor_section` is in `locus_body` (TELL, BREACH, SUBSIDING) or in the record's own body (CALM). One `lux(ref)` read per candidate per run, zero probes. **The target rule, stated plainly** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a candidate is *lit* when its total light `lux_pm(s) >= LIT_ON_PM` (150, CITED), a stateless comparison on the same quantity the argmax uses (the comparison is made fresh every run and nothing is stored; there is no off-threshold and no hysteresis, as for the Emitter's `probe` `lit_on`). **Horror does not gate on the Emitter's `lit` bit**: that bit is a hysteresis on `act_lux_pm`, which excludes the owner's own beam (EM-2, EM-21, EM AC-16a), so a lone player in the dark with the lamp on reads `lux_pm` 1000 but `act_lux_pm` 0 and would never be a candidate; the Emitter's own wording ("Horror sees a lit player", EM line 685) is the contract. Any light that raises `lux_pm` counts, including a fixture (the self-powered status glow of a docked pod's dock-room prop is an ordinary lit fixture by user ruling X2, so a seat at the dock console is a lit candidate and Horror adds no exception for it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*), a node lantern, a Chemlight pool, another crewmate's beam and the BEACON's sweep (the BEACON does not gate actions but does count in `lux_pm`; a seat swept by it is lit for as long as `lux_pm` stays at or above the threshold, and because P locks at REACH start a flapping lit state cannot steer a strike). **A seat standing in fixture light is lit and can be targeted with its own lamp off**; going dark means leaving the light, not only switching the lamp off (HE-26). The target is the lit candidate with the highest `lux_pm`, ties lowest seat id. **The argmax is therefore degenerate among seats whose own lamp is on**: each reads 1000 (the owner stands in their own light, EM-21), so the lowest seat id wins; the argmax discriminates only among seats lit by *other* light (fixtures, pools, a teammate's beam), and it is the presence of light, not its amount, that draws the horror. If no candidate is lit, the target is the locus section's anchor (the anchor REACH of HE-16). **The preference is recomputed every run and never stored.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The *walk* it leads to is committed, the target is not: the chosen goal waypoint is held in the persisted `goal_wp` for `GOAL_COMMIT_RUNS` runs (12, 60 ticks) unless it is reached, its seat leaves the candidate set, the phase changes, the layout changes or the goal becomes unreachable, so a lone seat on a lux boundary or under an L3 dip cannot make the stalk dither at 12 Hz (the layer players read as "it was hunting me"); REACH begin (HE-14) always reads the fresh target. The horror moves identically lit or unlit and is never repelled, stunned, slowed or harmed by light. This GDD **adopts the Emitter's text verbatim**, as the second GDD to land: "No beam stuns, burns, repels or damages a horror or a crewmate ... being revealed is the beam's whole effect" (EM:89). Objects are never targets at MVP: a dropped glowstick is a Chemlight pool that counts as exposure to whoever stands in it, but it is not a seat, so it does not pull the horror toward itself; flares, torches and decoys that repel or distract are Vertical Slice (EM:89). *Why.* Pillar 3 made legible ("you lit up, it came") with no meter. With two or more lit seats a stateless argmax can alternate; a hysteresis would need a stored value, which is a Vertical Slice question (Open Questions). *Cites.* EM:89, EM-21.
175	
176	**HE-14. REACH: the telegraph (unfold).** *Rule.* STALK → REACH begins at a run when **all** of the following hold: (a) `phase` is BREACH; (b) the target is a lit seat, or the anchor under HE-16; (c) `exogenous_permitted(actor_section(target seat))` holds for a seat REACH, and `exogenous_permitted(anchor section)` holds for an anchor REACH; (d) the distance from the horror's foot point to the point is at most `REACH_RANGE_PX`; (e) `T >= cooldown_until_T`; **(f) `connected(horror foot, P)`** (HE-19): the horror's foot point and P are in the same room (Layout `room_at`), or the two rooms are adjacent through an open, passable leaf (Layout `door_passage`, HE-19) whose hinge-aware `gap_rect` the straight segment from the foot point to P crosses *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. A Euclidean distance through a wall is not a reach: a horror one tile behind a wall from a lit seat begins no REACH, and the same pair across an open sill does *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: condition (d) alone let a REACH start through solid wall and strike nothing, a telegraph drawn through a wall for a lethal mechanic, which breaks P2's "a careful player could have perceived and had somewhere to run")*. The same condition (f) gates the anchor REACH (HE-16 (3)). At that run it **locks** the point P (the target seat's foot point; non-tracking) and draws `UNFOLD_TICKS = 5 × ceil_div(rng_int(UNFOLD_LO/5, UNFOLD_HI/5) × UNFOLD_SCALE_PCT, 100)` (integer order of operations: draw, multiply by the scale, `ceil_div`, then × 5) from `rng_derive(world_seed, "horror.tell", threat_counter(counter))` (`threat_counter` is the kernel's one restore-epoch derivation, HE-42) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)* (`UNFOLD_SCALE_PCT` is the accessibility lengthening of HE-F5, default 100, persisted in `horror.state`; it is applied after the draw, never shortens, and does not change the draw count) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the counter increments in the same block write, is persisted and restored exactly, and a restore never rerolls a REACH already in flight (its length is the stored `reach_end_T`; a REACH that later fizzles has still consumed its draw); the next REACH after a restore draws at the restored counter with the restore's new `restore_epoch` inside `threat_counter` (HE-42) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)* The body is rooted for the whole REACH; the limb extends toward P; `reach_end_T = reach_start_T + UNFOLD_TICKS` is a multiple of 5, so the strike resolves exactly on a run. During REACH the record publishes `state`, `locked_pt` and `reach_end_T` in `horror.view` (the rig and Audio read them). `UNFOLD_LO` and `UNFOLD_HI` must be multiples of 5 (data lint). The picture is the warning: the rig's reach-limb tip rests on P for the last part of the unfold (Visual/Audio Requirements), and the telegraph is **the limb entering the cone before the body**; no icon, ring, arc, disc, radius or ground decal marks the strike point. **The tip rests on P, which is the victim's own foot point, inside the victim's own light (EM-21: the owner stands in their own light), so the tip is lit for the victim wherever the body stands**; a touch-down SMEAR is laid at P at the start of the **hold stage** (`hold_start_T = reach_end_T − 5 × floor(3 × (UNFOLD_TICKS / 5) / 10)`, the last 25 to 50 ticks, when the tip rests on P; a true mark and a ring entry, not a marker) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: it is laid late on purpose, because a ground cue at REACH start would be a second, unacknowledged warning beside the limb and would weaken the blind-legibility claim (the limb alone carries the telegraph); a REACH that fizzles before the hold stage lays no smear, and `reach_start_T` and `locked_pt` stay observable in `horror.view` and the debug record so replay and TellAudit still see when the REACH began; Audio renders a positional REACH cue from `locked_pt`: a non-percussive lead-in started `REACH_RESOLVE_PRE_TICKS` 90 before `reach_end_T` (registry `reach_resolve_start`, `REACH_RESOLVE_PRE_TICKS <= UNFOLD_LO`) and ending at `reach_end_T` with no impact transient (Audio AA-28 b). There is **no lit-self gate**: the horror moves identically lit or unlit (HE-13). The point is locked at the start and never updated, so moving out of the strike disc (HE-15) always works. If the blind-legibility acceptance criterion fails, the fallback is a larger `UNFOLD_LO` or a smaller `R_SNAP_PX`, never a victim-side marker (a marker is a HUD by another name, Pillar 3). *(orchestrator ruling: checkpoint CP-1; C-HE-9 closed.)* *Why.* ART 5.4 ("a limb entering the cone before the body"), Pillar 2; a tracking strike is learnable never. *Cites.* HE-F2, HE-F5, ART:540.
177	
178	**HE-15. STRIKE: bodily resolution.** *Rule.* At the first run with `T >= reach_end_T` and the predicate satisfied, the state becomes STRIKE for `STRIKE_HOLD_RUNS` runs (the snap pose; no travel). 286	The record's `state` takes one of six values: `LURK`, `STALK`, `REACH`, `STRIKE`, `RETREAT`, `TRANSIT`. The first five are the cycle; `TRANSIT` is a **sixth value, additive** to the five the audio facts need (C-HE-17): relocation through a hull needs a visible place in the machine and has no position. "Permitted act" is what the state may do to the world. Dormancy (HE-21) is not a state: a record whose body is unloaded is frozen in whatever state it holds, with no step.
287	
288	#### State table
289	
290	| State | Entry (from, guard) | Phases it lives in | Permitted act | Registered subject | Motion | Exit (first match wins) | Who may cause the transition |
291	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
292	| **LURK** | boot or default; STALK on a TELL abort; RETREAT when the phase is CALM or TELL and the record is not returning; TRANSIT arrival while the phase is CALM | CALM (any other phase only transiently) | marks, CHILL, disturbance dips; no RUPTURE, no GOUGE, no suit damage; never within `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` of a living seat | yes | `V_CREEP_MPX` between waypoints; dwell `LURK_DWELL_TICKS` | `attention.view.phase` = TELL with a new `tell_epoch` → STALK (locus body is its body) or TRANSIT (another body; evaluated first, so it fires even when the record's own body is unloaded); return due → TRANSIT; body unloaded and the locus body is its own or none → frozen *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | **Attention's phase only** (HE-7); never the player's light, noise or distance |
293	| **STALK** | LURK on TELL entry; RETREAT when the cooldown has elapsed in BREACH; TRANSIT arrival in TELL or BREACH | TELL, BREACH | marks, CHILL, disturbance. TELL: the standoff holds, no harm. BREACH: may begin a REACH under HE-14 | yes | TELL `V_CREEP_MPX`; BREACH `V_HUNT_MPX` | TELL abort (phase back to CALM) → LURK; BREACH and HE-14 (a) to (f) true → REACH; SUBSIDING → RETREAT; no lit seat → the anchor becomes the target (still STALK) | `attention.view` fields and the stateless `lux_pm >= LIT_ON_PM` read of HE-13 (not the Emitter's `lit` bit); the abort is Attention's *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
294	| **REACH** | STALK in BREACH when the predicate holds at begin | BREACH (resolves in BREACH or SUBSIDING) | lays the touch-down SMEAR at P at the start of the hold stage (a pre-hold fizzle lays none, HE-14); publishes `reach_start_T`, `locked_pt` and `reach_end_T`; no harm yet; rooted | yes | none | `T >= reach_end_T` and the predicate holds → STRIKE; the predicate false at that run, or the phase CALM, or a restore with the predicate false → RETREAT (fizzle: no harm, no hairlines, no GOUGE or RUPTURE, no cooldown; an already-laid touch-down smear stays); `SUBSIDE_CANCELS_REACH` 1 and SUBSIDING → RETREAT (fizzle) | the predicate (Attention's `exogenous_permitted`); the horror's own clock |

296	| **RETREAT** | STRIKE; a fizzle; SUBSIDING entry; (Vertical Slice) a `repel` | BREACH, SUBSIDING, then CALM | marks only | yes | `V_CREEP_MPX` away from every living seat | `T >= cooldown_until_T` and BREACH → STALK; CALM or TELL and not returning → LURK; return due → TRANSIT | Attention's phase; the horror's own clock |
297	| **TRANSIT** | TELL entry with `body_of(locus_section_id)` not its own (also from an unloaded body, HE-20); return due (`RETURN_DELAY_TICKS`); its section lost to a cut (HE-22) | any | none; no position, no marks (the egress and ingress marks are laid at the segments, not by the traveller), not registered | no | none | `T >= transit_until_T` and a legal entry (HE-20) → STALK (TELL or BREACH), LURK (CALM) or RETREAT (SUBSIDING), with E6 and an ingress mark; a TELL abort while outbound cancels the arrival and retargets to `from_body_id` (HE-20); a new `tell_epoch` retargets to the new locus body *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Attention's locus; Layout for legality |
298	
299	#### Phase view (state against phase: the single table a reviewer tests against)
300	
301	| Phase | LURK | STALK | REACH | STRIKE | RETREAT | TRANSIT |
302	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
303	| CALM | resident | → LURK (after an abort) | fizzle | n/a | → LURK | an abort cancels an outbound arrival (the record heads back; it never arrives as LURK from an abort) |
304	| TELL | → STALK | creep, standoff holds, no harm | cannot begin | n/a | → LURK | arrives as STALK |
305	| BREACH | n/a | hunt; may begin a REACH | the telegraph | harm (predicate) | cooldown | arrives as STALK |
306	| SUBSIDING | n/a | → RETREAT | resolves or fizzles | harm only if resolving | stays | arrives as RETREAT |

308	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the CALM/TRANSIT cell no longer reads "arrives as LURK" after an abort, HE-20; a TRANSIT record that reached its arrival run in CALM for any other reason, such as a return home completing, still arrives as LURK.)*
309	
310	A TELL abort moves the phase from TELL to CALM; the record in STALK returns to LURK with no strike and no mark burst (HE-12). A record in RETREAT during a second TELL goes RETREAT → LURK → STALK on the new `tell_epoch`; it never skips LURK. Predicate check points (each is an acceptance criterion): REACH begin (HE-14 c), STRIKE entry (HE-15), every M17 RUPTURE or GOUGE call (HE-16, HE-29). All three read `exogenous_permitted` at their own tick. CHILL is a non-harm footprint, permitted in any phase, bounded by HE-F4 and HE-31 (C-HE-28).
311	
312	#### Transition guards (ordered; the first match wins within a run)
313	
314	1. **Restore-first.** A run that follows a restore re-checks the predicate for any record in REACH (HE-41) before any other guard.
315	2. **Tell edge (new `tell_epoch`; runs for every record in every run, ahead of dormancy)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; was guard 4, which sat behind dormancy so a record whose body was unloaded never saw the edge)*. If `tell_epoch != last_seen_tell_epoch`: zero the five epoch counters and empty `gouged_seg_ids`, set `last_seen_tell_epoch := tell_epoch`, and take a record in REACH to a fizzle (HE-17: no harm, no cooldown consumed) and a record in STRIKE out of its hold, each going to RETREAT in this run (a new `tell_epoch` means the previous breach is over) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; then LURK → STALK (the locus body is the record's body; a record found in RETREAT or STALK passes through LURK first, never skipping it, E-HE-16) or LURK / STALK / RETREAT → TRANSIT (another body; a departure from an unloaded body is allowed, HE-20, and is the only act an unloaded record performs); a record already in TRANSIT retargets to the new locus body (HE-20). Nothing else in the run may act on the record before this check.
316	3. **Dormancy** *(after the registration reconciliation of HE-34, which runs between guards 2 and 3)*. The record's body is not loaded and the record is not in TRANSIT → no step (HE-21). (A TRANSIT record has no body; its wait for an unloaded destination is HE-21's second rule.)
317	4. **Layout change.** `layout.state` changed since the last run, or `version(section_id)` changed for a section of the record's body (a door opened or closed) → first the door-eject check of HE-26 (a leaf closed on the horror's foot box), then invalidate the path cache and re-derive `body_id` from `body_of(section_id)` (HE-22) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
318	5. **Phase edge (the rest).** The phase returned to CALM from TELL (an abort) → STALK → LURK, or an outbound TRANSIT (`transit_leg` OUTBOUND) is cancelled and retargeted to `from_body_id` with `transit_leg` RETURN (HE-20); SUBSIDING → STALK → RETREAT. A record in REACH or STRIKE is untouched by this guard (guard 6 resolves it).
319	6. **Cycle guards** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **Independent of phase:** REACH → STRIKE or fizzle at `T >= reach_end_T` (a REACH begun in BREACH resolves in SUBSIDING, HE-17, and fizzles in CALM or when `SUBSIDE_CANCELS_REACH` is 1) and STRIKE → RETREAT after `STRIKE_HOLD_RUNS`. **In BREACH only:** STALK → REACH (HE-14) and RETREAT → STALK.
320	7. **Return.** `RETURN_DELAY_TICKS` after the end of SUBSIDING or a TELL abort and not in the home body → TRANSIT.
321	
322	**Epoch counters.** `strikes_epoch`, `gouges_epoch`, `ruptures_epoch`, `chill_epoch_dj` and `chill_deposits_epoch` reset **lazily, keyed on the comparison `tell_epoch != last_seen_tell_epoch` and not on observing the phase edge itself**: at the first run in which a record sees that inequality (guard 2, which runs first), the five counters are zeroed, `gouged_seg_ids` is emptied and `last_seen_tell_epoch` is updated before any act in that run. A record that slept through one or more TELLs, or a save restored from an older epoch, therefore wakes with zero counters and its caps bind correctly. Caps bound each told epoch, and CALM activity after a breach counts against that epoch's remaining allowance until the next TELL. `epoch_id` (HE-41) is set to the new `tell_epoch` at the same moment *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
323	
324	#### Published fields by state (`horror.view`)
325	
326	| State | Published beyond the always-present `entity_id`, `type_id`, `state`, `body_id`, `section_id`, `pos_px` |
327	|---|---|
328	| LURK, STALK, RETREAT | `state_enter_T`; the disturbance list; diagnostic counters |
329	| REACH | `reach_start_T`, `locked_pt`, `reach_end_T` (the rig and Audio read them; the player reads the limb; `reach_start_T` keeps replay and TellAudit able to see when the REACH began although the smear is laid later) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |

331	| TRANSIT | `transit_until_T`, `transit_leg`, the pending ingress segment once chosen; no `pos_px` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |

The timers: `state_enter_T`, `reach_start_T`, `reach_end_T`, `cooldown_until_T`, `transit_until_T`, `ingress_mark_T`, `dwell_start_T`, `strike_T` and `last_seen_tell_epoch`. The counters: the `"horror.tell"` counter, `fp_count` for `fp_window`, the per-epoch ledgers (`strikes_epoch`, `gouges_epoch`, `ruptures_epoch`, `chill_epoch_dj`, `chill_deposits_epoch`, `gouged_seg_ids`), `hold_runs`, `blocked_runs`, `goal_commit_runs`, `smear_travel_px`, `chill_travel_px`, `lurk_dwell_index` and the `mark_id` counter. The mark ring with each mark's `life_left_ticks`, and the disturbance list with `last_end_T`. A restore reconstructs every state from these, never from the previous process's memory (G4 save-equivalence, given the pair (save, `restore_epoch`)); the committed field manifest (AC-HE-76) is the check that this list and HE-41 stay one list *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.

337	#### Cycle timing at the placeholders
338	
339	Minimum interval between two strike resolutions for a seat that has not moved is `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + UNFOLD_LO` = 395 ticks (6.6 s) when the horror is already in reach range. `UNFOLD_TICKS` is `5 × rng_int(19, 36)`: 18 equally likely values from 95 to 180 with mean 137.5, so the mean interval is 437.5 ticks (7.3 s) and the longest is 480 ticks (8.0 s). That is a lower bound: after a strike the horror retreats (96 ticks out at `V_CREEP_MPX`, inside the cooldown), turns at `cooldown_until_T` and walks back at `V_HUNT_MPX` (64 ticks, 65 on the run grid), so the realised period of a seat that does not move is `UNFOLD_TICKS + STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + 65` = 460 to 545 ticks (7.7 to 9.1 s), mean 502.5 (registered formula HE-F15). The time to a third strike for a seat that never moves, and the share of minimum-length breaches that contain a third REACH start (none), are derived in HE-F16 and are not carried here.

248

Its acceptance criteria read **NOT ASSESSED at MVP, never PASS**. **Conflict C-HE-6 — closed. Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): Option A (X6).** The start kit carried `tool_suppressant` with `SUPPRESSANT_START_CHARGES` 3 and no effect, a Pillar 1 problem of its own (a tool whose use changes nothing in the world is a lie the sane game tells). `tool_suppressant` is removed from the MVP start kit (SE-11 slot 4, SE-14, SE-15), from the Item DB MVP list and from the HUD, and returns with its effect verb at Vertical Slice; the registry name `SUPPRESSANT_START_CHARGES` is retired (status deprecated). 251	**HE-40. Rig presenter, Sanity and the Perception Filter.** *Rule.* A render-side rig presenter takes `(pose_stream, type_id)` and an optional `leak` input that **only the Filter may set**; Horror feeds it real poses with `leak` 0; the Filter (Vertical Slice) may feed phantom or crewmate-driven poses (ART:594 "0 extra frames"; class (c) is driven by the crewmate's true velocity and true beam). A rig instance with no Horror ref in `horror.view` and `leak` 0 is a lint error. Sanity's rulings decide what Horror owes: keep every real entity registered (E6) with a true anchor and publish true positions in `horror.view`; Horror computes no exposure, owns neither `HORROR_NEAR_R` (called `HORROR_SEEN_R` in the Sanity rulings; renamed in the Sanity draft, C-HE-32) nor `EXP_HORROR`, and holds no sanity reference. -> ADR candidate (3). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: Sanity and the Perception Filter are both `Status: Designed`.)* *Cites.* PIPE:303, PCI row 16, ART:594, SN-22.

253	#### Group I — State, determinism and budget
254	
255	**HE-41. Block contents and restore.** *Rule.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The field list was incomplete: a restore could not reproduce the uninterrupted run. The list below is the closed manifest, committed as a file and checked by AC-HE-76 (the old criterion checked the implementation against its own list, which is how the gaps passed review twice). Persisted per record, in groups. (1) *Identity and place:* an in-block `entity_id` counter, `type_id`, `body_id`, `home_body_id`, `section_id`, `pos_px`, `acc_mpx` (the two-axis sub-pixel residue), `last_octant`, `exo_source_class` (the EXOGENOUS class of the record's `source_ref`, set once at creation, HE-15), and `offset_seen_px` (an int2: the `section_offset(section_id)` this record last used for its body-frame points, written at creation (E6 time), at every run and at ingress; HE-22 re-bases on a mismatch) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. (2) *Behaviour and timers:* `state`, `state_enter_T`, `cooldown_until_T`, `last_seen_tell_epoch`, `epoch_id`. Block-level: the mark ring (each mark with its `life_left_ticks`) and the `mark_id` counter, the `"horror.tell"` counter, `fp_window` and `fp_count`, the active disturbance list and the `last_end_T` map (bounded by `L3_MAX_TRACKED`), `lurk_dwell_index`, and `unfold_scale_pct` (the accessibility scale of HE-14, applied after the draw; sim-visible, changed only by the host command of HE-F5, and replays with the world). **Not persisted:** the target, any threat of any kind (none exists), the path cache, `restore_epoch` (Save/Load's value in `slot_epoch.bin`, read through `kernel.clock`, HE-42; *Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14*) and the non-hashed `horror.view.debug` record of HE-7. A restore **into REACH** keeps the full remaining telegraph (never shortened; mirrors AT E-51) and re-checks the predicate; if it no longer holds, RETREAT with no strike. A restore into TRANSIT with `transit_until_T` in the past is legal (arrive next run); a TRANSIT record with a registered subject, or a non-TRANSIT record without a legal section, is `STATE_INCOHERENT`. All explicit dirty keys; plain data only, no `StringName` keys or `Vector2i`; restore is idempotent. -> ADR candidate (5). *Cites.* SL-15, SL:221-232, AT E-51.
256	
257	**HE-42. Determinism.** *Rule.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)* The two draw kernels (Attention's `restore_epoch` key and a Horror-private epoch seed) are replaced by the one below; Attention's AT-8 calls the same function. All simulation randomness is `rng_derive(world_seed, "horror.tell", counter_eff)`, used for the REACH length only, where `counter_eff = threat_counter(counter)` and **`threat_counter(c) = c + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE × restore_epoch` is the kernel's one derivation for threat draws** (the stream-name hash stays cached and unchanged; Attention and Horror call it and neither defines its own). `restore_epoch` is a persisted u32 **owned by Save/Load** (starts at 0), held in the per-slot side file `slot_epoch.bin` (u32 + CRC32, written atomically by temp file and rename by the Save/Load worker); it is in no generation file, so generation bytes and every trailer SHA never change, and each generation header carries only a read-only copy for recovery (R14). A death-stub restore advances it by 1; a Continue of a `QUIT` generation that is the newest non-demoted verified generation carries it unchanged (R13, user ruling D16: not steerable by quit); a Continue of any other generation (after a kill, crash or fallback), in-process or after a fresh process start, advances it. Save/Load writes an advance in a pre-restore staging step and calls `request_restore(gen, restore_epoch)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`; on a failed write or after `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500 ms placeholder) it proceeds with the advanced epoch in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED` (a listed exposure: a kill before a later successful write may replay that epoch once). So two death restores of one autosave give two new epochs, and a Save & Quit then Continue replays the same REACH lengths: quit-and-continue is no reroll oracle *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14; cross-GDD fix)*. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)`, sim-visible and pure. `RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` is 1,048,576 (2^20) and is the kernel's constant (registry request: its source moves from Attention to the kernel, with Attention, Horror and Save/Load in `referenced_by`); the lint `counter < RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` holds. Horror reads `restore_epoch` through `threat_counter` at the draw and at no other time, never stores it in `horror.state` and never decides when it advances; the Graph's physical failures and every persisted counter never read it. The persisted `"horror.tell"` counter is restored exactly, so no draw is reused at one epoch and the counter never moves backwards, and a REACH already in flight keeps its stored length (`reach_end_T`, E-HE-36). **Determinism (G4) is defined given the pair (save bytes, `restore_epoch`)**: the same pair replays identically (strike lengths, positions, marks, `state_hash`), tests pin the epoch, and a restore that advances the epoch changes only the lengths of REACHes not yet begun. Nothing physical is re-keyed: mark seeds, LURK waypoint choice and L3 timing are pure integer hashes of ids, the run index and `HE_HASH_SEED` through `he_hash` (below), so the trail and the positions the player can read in the world replay exactly (Pillar 1); they are not threat draws, since the REACH length is Horror's only draw. No wall clock and no global RNG (H9). **`he_hash`** *(defined 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier text said "pure integer hash" with no function or sign rule)*: `he_hash(k1, k2, k3, salt) = lsr(mix64( mix64(k1 ⊕ HE_HASH_SEED) ⊕ mix64(k2 ⊕ salt) ⊕ (k3 × GOLDEN) ), 1)`, on the kernel's pinned `mix64`, `lsr` and `GOLDEN` (kernel D.10) with the intended wrap on the multiplication; the final logical shift makes the result non-negative (63 bits), so every `mod` in this GDD acts on a non-negative integer and no reduction depends on a sign convention. `HE_HASH_SEED` defaults to `0x4845` (any fixed integer; changing it re-rolls every mark seed, LURK waypoint and L3 timing). The salts are fixed constants: `SALT_MARK` 1, `SALT_WP` 2, `SALT_L3_START` 3, `SALT_L3_STRENGTH` 4, `SALT_L3_DUR` 5. Callers: mark seed `he_hash(mark_id, 0, 0, SALT_MARK)`; waypoint rank `he_hash(entity_id, dwell_index, anchor_local_key, SALT_WP)`; L3 `h1`, `h2`, `h3` = `he_hash(emitter_id, run_n, 0, SALT_L3_START)`, `…SALT_L3_STRENGTH)`, `…SALT_L3_DUR)`. Golden vectors are pinned by AC-HE-139. -> ADR candidate (4): a shared pure-integer presentation hash with Lighting LO-19. *Cites.* KRN D.10, D.12, H9.

513	### HE-F6 Speed cadence and the escape invariant
514	
515	The speed cadence and escape invariant formula is defined as:
516	
517	`acc ← acc + V_MPX;  v_eff = floor(acc / 1000);  acc ← acc − 1000 × v_eff   (once per tick of a run);   V_CREEP_MPX < V_HUNT_MPX < V_WALK × 1000;   ceil(V_MPX / 1000) ≤ 3`
518	
519	**Variables:**
520	
521	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
522	|---|---|---|---|---|
523	| `V_MPX` | int milli-px/tick | `V_CREEP_MPX` or `V_HUNT_MPX` | Horror | Speed of the current state: LURK, STALK in a TELL, RETREAT and the arrival walk use `V_CREEP_MPX`; STALK in BREACH uses `V_HUNT_MPX` |
524	| `V_CREEP_MPX` ★ | int | 1000..1400, [PH] 1000 | Horror | Below 1000 a tick can have `v_eff` 0, and Body resets its sub-pixel residue on a zero-speed tick (BDY-12), so the floor stays 1000 until that is verified |
525	| `V_HUNT_MPX` ★ | int | `V_CREEP_MPX`+1..1999, [PH] 1500 | Horror | Approach speed in BREACH |
526	| `V_WALK` | int px/tick | 2 (CITED) | Player Controller | A walking seat, including a CRITICAL walk-only seat |
527	| `acc` | int | 0..999 | block, per record | Persisted remainder |
528	| `v_eff` | int px/tick | 1..3 | this formula | The per-tick step passed to Body's `LocomotionStep` with the run's octant |
529	
530	**Output Range:** `v_eff` in 1..2 at the placeholders; the sweep box of Body's step is sized for 3 (BDY-15). The invariant means a walker gains `V_WALK × 1000 − V_HUNT_MPX = 500` milli-px per tick on a hunter. A **carrier** (`V_CARRY` 1, 1000 milli-px) cannot out-walk `V_HUNT_MPX` (HE-24, C-HE-8).
531	
532	**Example:** `V_HUNT_MPX` 1500, `acc = 0`: run one steps 1, 2, 1, 2, 1 = 7 px (`acc` 500); run two steps 2, 1, 2, 1, 2 = 8 px; mean 7.5 px per run, 1.5 px/tick, 90 px/s. `V_CREEP_MPX` 1000: always 1, 5 px per run, `acc` stays 0. A walker at 2 px/tick gains 0.5 px/tick on the hunter: 30 px/s.
533	
534	**Registry candidate:** `horror_speed_invariant`.

536	### HE-F7 Mark ring eviction, lifetime and ageing
537	
538	The mark ring eviction, lifetime and ageing formula is defined as:
539	
540	`insert of kind K at its quota evicts argmin(mark_id) over kind = K;   insert of a SMEAR into a full ring evicts argmin(mark_id) over kind = SMEAR;   n_other_max = MARK_QUOTA_RIME + MARK_QUOTA_HAIRLINES + MARK_QUOTA_STRUCK;   life_left ← life_left − HORROR_RUN_TICKS per run while the mark's section is loaded, removed at life_left ≤ 0;   stage = min(2, floor(3 × (MARK_LIFE_TICKS − life_left) / MARK_LIFE_TICKS));   smear_retention_ticks = (MAX_MARKS − n_other_max) × MARK_SPACING_PX × 1000 / V_CREEP_MPX;   MARK_LIFE_TICKS ≥ smear_retention_ticks ≥ TRAIL_TARGET_TICKS;   MAX_MARKS − n_other_max ≥ ceil(TRAIL_TARGET_TICKS × V_CREEP_MPX / (MARK_SPACING_PX × 1000))` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*

543	
544	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
545	|---|---|---|---|---|
546	| `mark_id` | int | ≥ 1, never reused | block counter | Insertion order |
547	| `kind` | enum | SMEAR, RIME, HAIRLINES, STRUCK | block | Mark kind (HE-27) |
548	| `MAX_MARKS` | int | `n_other_max + 19`..48 (32..48 at the placeholders), [PH] 32 | Horror | Ring size. Raised from 24 to 32 in the design review (at 24 the smear history was `(24 − 9) × 96 = 1440` ticks, below the 1800 target); the range's floor now follows the quotas, so the range no longer contradicts its own relation *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; a registry request |

551	| `CHILL_SPACING_PX` | int px | 192..768, [PH] 384 | Horror | One CHILL deposit and rime mark per this much travel, and at each LURK dwell start |

The rime quota is `ceil(MAX_MARKS / (CHILL_SPACING_PX / MARK_SPACING_PX + 1))` = `ceil(32 / 5)` = 7 (one rime per five ring slots of creep); the other two follow the three-strike ladder. Asserted at data load as arithmetic (`n_other_max + 19 <= MAX_MARKS`), never as a runtime-derived fixture *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
553	| `MARK_QUOTA_RIME` / `MARK_QUOTA_HAIRLINES` / `MARK_QUOTA_STRUCK` | int | 1..12 / 1..6 / 1..6, [PH] 7 / 3 / 3, and `sum + 19 <= MAX_MARKS` | Horror | Per-kind ring quotas (HE-30); an insert at quota evicts the oldest of its own kind *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
554	| `TRAIL_TARGET_TICKS` | int ticks | 1800..3600, [PH] 1800 | game-designer target (the hidden-entity investigation window), not a runtime value | The trail an investigator arriving up to 30 s late should still find |
555	| `V_CREEP_MPX` | int | 1000 | HE-F6 | Creep speed |
556	| `MARKS_PER_RUN_MAX` | int | 1..4, [PH] 2 | Horror | Inserts per run; over the cap, priority STRUCK, then HAIRLINES, then RIME, then SMEAR; a dropped insert is counted `horror_marks_withheld` |
557	
558	**Output Range:** `stage` in {0, 1, 2}: exactly three frame stages for smear and rime (and two for hairlines), so physical age is readable without a meter (Pillar 1) and no continuous value is drawn. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* `smear_retention_ticks` is now a **guaranteed minimum**, because the quotas fix `n_other_max` at 13: at the placeholders `(32 − 13) × 96 × 1000 / 1000 = 1824` ticks at creep speed, at or above `TRAIL_TARGET_TICKS` 1800 whatever the history (an 18000-tick CALM LURK fills the rime quota and no more; a 3600-tick breach fills the HAIRLINES and STRUCK quotas and no more, the oldest of a kind being replaced); more smear history, up to 2112 ticks with only ten others resident, is available but not guaranteed. At `V_HUNT_MPX` the same ring holds `19 × 96 × 1000 / 1500 = 1216` ticks, below the target: the BREACH approach trail is short-lived by construction (the horror covers distance faster than a smear can age), the hidden-entity investigation window is defined on the creep trail, and the shortfall is accepted and logged (Open Question 20). The touch-down SMEAR of each REACH is a SMEAR and competes with the travel smears, but REACHes occur only in BREACH, where that shortfall is already accepted. The ring, not the lifetime, is the binding bound on a creeping horror; the lifetime exists so a frozen loaded body does not keep stale marks forever.
559	
560	**Example:** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* the ring is full at 32 with 3 hairline marks, 3 STRUCK marks, 7 rime marks and 19 smears. A new smear evicts the oldest smear and never a hairline; a fourth HAIRLINES mark evicts the oldest HAIRLINES mark and nothing else; an eighth rime evicts the oldest rime. There is always a smear to evict because `32 > 13`. The relation `MAX_MARKS − n_other_max >= ceil(TRAIL_TARGET_TICKS × V_CREEP_MPX / (MARK_SPACING_PX × 1000))` = 19 is an arithmetic assertion the data load makes: `13 + 19 = 32` passes, and a quota set summing to 14 with `MAX_MARKS` 32 fails the load. Ageing: a mark with `life_left` 12000 has age 6000 and `stage = floor(3 × 6000 / 18000) = 1`; at `life_left` 5999 the age is 12001 and the stage is 2.

565	
566	The target selection formula is defined as:
567	
568	`candidates = { s : living(s) ∧ ¬DOWNED(s) ∧ ¬IN_POD(s) ∧ actor_section(s) ∈ body_scope ∧ lit(s) };   target = argmax over candidates of (lux_pm(s), −seat_id);   candidates = ∅ ⇒ target = ANCHOR (HE-16 (3))`

573	
574	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
575	|---|---|---|---|---|
576	| `lux_pm(s)` | int permille | 0..1000 | Emitter `lux(ref)` | The seat's illumination; the owner stands in their own light (EM-21), so a seat with its lamp on reads 1000 |
577	| `lit(s)` | bool | — | derived here: `lux_pm(s) >= LIT_ON_PM` (150, CITED) | Stateless, recomputed every run, nothing stored. **Not the Emitter's `lit` bit** (a hysteresis on `act_lux_pm`, which excludes the owner's own beam and the BEACON; a lone lamp-on player reads `act_lux_pm` 0) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
