587	### HE-F9 Ingress timing and entry choice
588	
589	The ingress timing and entry choice formula is defined as:
590	
591	`transit_until_T = tell_enter_T + INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS;   fallback_T = transit_until_T + STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR_TICKS;   arrive_T = min{ T ≥ transit_until_T : T mod 5 = 0 ∧ ( legal_entry(T) ∨ (T ≥ fallback_T + INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS ∧ fallback_entry(T)) ) };   stalk_visible_min = TELL_MIN_TICKS − INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS;   D_entry_max = LURK_STANDOFF_PX + floor(stalk_visible_min × V_CREEP_MPX / 1000);   INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS + STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR_TICKS + INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS ≤ TELL_MIN_TICKS` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
592	
593	`legal_entry(T)` selects, among the hull entries of `locus_body` at room-hop distance 1 from the room of the highest-`lux_pm` living seat (none lit or present: the locus section's outermost compartment), a hull segment whose room holds no living seat and which lies at least `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` from every living seat **that is `linked` to it (HE-19)**; ties lowest hop, then lowest room id, then lowest hull-segment id. A *hull entry* is an `anchor_geometry` point of a hull-bearing compartment that lies within `HULL_CONTACT_PX` of a hull face, paired with the lowest id returned by `hull_segments_near(section_id, anchor_px, HULL_CONTACT_PX)`; there is no `solid_in` sampling and no unpublished room-to-segment read. The entry is chosen at the run at `transit_until_T − INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS` and the ingress mark is laid then (re-chosen under E-HE-34 if it becomes illegal); the body arrives at `transit_until_T`, or at the first later run whose re-chosen entry has had its full mark lead. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Fallback.** `fallback_entry(T)` is the *nearest legal hull anchor*: if no legal entry exists at `fallback_T` (540 ticks after TELL entry at the placeholders, inside `TELL_MIN_TICKS`), the hop-1 and standoff conditions drop out and the entry is the hull entry nearest by room hops to the lit seat's room whose room holds no living seat (ties as above); its mark is laid at `fallback_T` and the body arrives `INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS` later, no later than `TELL_MIN_TICKS`. Only when every hull room holds a living seat does the record stay in TRANSIT (`horror_ingress_pending`, E-HE-33). **Precondition of `stalk_visible_min`:** the visible-stalk bound below holds only when a legal entry exists at `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS`; under the fallback the told breach still has a horror and an ingress mark from `fallback_T`, but the visible stalk can be as short as the mark lead before BREACH entry at the shortest tell.
594	
595	**Variables:**
596	
597	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
598	|---|---|---|---|---|
599	| `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS` ★ | int ticks | 120..360, [PH] 300 | Horror | Earliest ingress after TELL entry |
600	| `TELL_MIN_TICKS` | int ticks | 600 (CITED, DERIVED from `W_MIN_WARNING_S`) | Attention, registry | Shortest tell |
601	| `STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR_TICKS` | int ticks | 120..360, [PH] 240 | Horror | The least visible stalk the design accepts |
602	| `INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS` | int ticks | 30..120, [PH] 60 | Horror | The mark precedes the body so a player watching that wall sees the arrival coming |
603	| `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` | int px | 144..288, [PH] 192 | Horror | HE-F14 |
604	| `V_CREEP_MPX` | int milli-px/tick | 1000..1400, [PH] 1000 | Horror | HE-F6 |
605	| `D_entry_max` | int px | derived 492 | this formula | The farthest an entry may lie from the seat for the stalk to close to the standoff before the shortest tell ends |

780	**Example:** `P(s_3 < B)` over the 18 × 18 equiprobable draw pairs: 0 at 900, 0.3 % at 990, 1.9 % at 1000, 28.1 % at 1050, 75.9 % at 1100, 99.7 % at 1155, 100 % at 1156. Session ratchet: `λ = 0.5` gives 1.4 %, `λ = 1.0` gives 8.0 % (the median target), `λ = 1.5` gives 19.1 %, `λ = 2.4` gives 43.0 %, `λ = 3.0` gives 57.7 %, `λ = 6.0` gives 93.8 %. The whole "death is a bitch" dial is the per-attempt miss rate `p`, set by telegraph legibility (HE-14), not by any number in the knob table.

784	### HE-F17 Hull act ladder gate
785	
786	The hull act ladder formula is defined as:
787	
788	`rupture_ok = (seg ∈ gouged_seg_ids) ∧ ruptures_epoch < RUPTURES_PER_EPOCH_MAX ∧ exogenous_permitted(section(seg)) ∧ hit_list = ∅;   gouge_ok = gouges_epoch < GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX ∧ exogenous_permitted(section(seg));   deposit(STRIKE at P within HULL_CONTACT_PX of seg) = RUPTURE if rupture_ok, else GOUGE if gouge_ok, else none;   on a GOUGE: gouged_seg_ids ← gouged_seg_ids ∪ {seg} (after the test above);   lint: STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS < min_gap = STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + UNFOLD_LO` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
789	
790	One hull deposit kind per STRIKE: the RUPTURE act is a later act than the GOUGE act it requires (HE-16 (2); *orchestrator ruling: HE-16 is silent on a strike where both are eligible, and one deposit per act keeps each act preceded by its own REACH*). The anchor REACH (no lit seat) may deposit one GOUGE only (`ANCHOR_REACH_GOUGES` 1), never RUPTURE. The kind is hull only (lint `GOUGE_NON_HULL`).
791	
792	**Variables:**
793	
794	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
795	|---|---|---|---|---|
796	| `gouges_epoch`, `ruptures_epoch` | int | 0..`GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX`, 0..`RUPTURES_PER_EPOCH_MAX` | block (reset lazily at the first run that sees a new `tell_epoch`, transition guard 2) | Hull acts this `tell_epoch` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
797	| `GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX` | int | 0..6, [PH] 3 | Horror | Hull GOUGE ceiling per epoch |
798	| `RUPTURES_PER_EPOCH_MAX` | int | 0..1, [PH] 1 | Horror | A RUPTURE needs a Graph-told clock afterwards (decompression, `RUPTURE_HP` 3600, registry, LSG:102) |
799	| `HULL_CONTACT_PX` | int px | 12..48, [PH] 24 | Horror | P within this of a hull-segment face |
800	| `gouged_seg_ids` | ascending int list | length at most `GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX` and at most `gouges_epoch` | block (emptied by guard 2) | The hull-segment ids this epoch's GOUGEs landed on: the whole gouge ledger the RUPTURE gate reads (ids only, no time) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
801	| `magnitude` | int bp | ≤ `FOOTPRINT_MAX_GOUGE_BP` 2500 (registry, LSG:914, CITED) | Graph | M17 magnitude |
802	
803	**Output Range:** per epoch at most 3 GOUGE and 1 RUPTURE, hence at most 4 hull-deposit M17 calls from strikes (plus the anchor GOUGE, which counts against `GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX`). The earlier time clause `T ≥ gouge_T + STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS` is **deleted** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: consecutive strikes are at least `min_gap` = `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + UNFOLD_LO` = 395 apart (HE-F15), which exceeds `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS` for any `UNFOLD_LO >= 1`, so the clause could never decide an outcome and a stored time would only add restore state. The ordering that matters, a GOUGE strictly earlier than the RUPTURE that needs it and never in the same strike (it forbids a same-act GOUGE-plus-RUPTURE and keeps the scrape ahead of the tear), is carried by membership in `gouged_seg_ids` tested before the append; the lint in the formula guards the one assumption it rests on.
804	
805	**Example:** a lit seat stands beside a hull face. Strike one at `T = 1075`: P within 24 px of segment S, no GOUGE yet: `deposit = GOUGE` (`gouges_epoch = 1`, S appended to `gouged_seg_ids`), radial hairlines laid. Strike two at `T = 1550` on S, the seat having walked out of the disc (`hit_list = ∅`): `rupture_ok` (S ∈ `gouged_seg_ids`, `ruptures_epoch 0 < 1`, nobody in the disc): `deposit = RUPTURE`; had the seat stood still and been struck, `rupture_ok` is false and the deposit is `GOUGE` (if under 3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Strike three on S: `ruptures_epoch = 1`, so `GOUGE` (if under 3). A GOUGE sets the segment `fatigued`, an ENDOGENOUS creep that outlives the breach and sits under the Graph's own `W_MIN_WARNING_S` gate (HE-16 (4)); Horror neither alters nor shortens it.
806	
807	**Registry candidate:** `hull_act_ladder`.

809	### HE-F18 Presentation interpolation alpha (render side only)
810	
811	The presentation interpolation alpha formula is defined as:
812	
813	`alpha5 = ((T_now − T_run) + tick_alpha) / HORROR_RUN_TICKS;   draw_pos = pos_prev + (pos_curr − pos_prev) × alpha5`
814	
815	This is presentation arithmetic (real numbers, never hashed, never in a SIM block); the rig *pose* is stepped once per run and never tweened (PIPE row 14). It is owed to the Pipeline because the kernel's `tick_alpha` spans one tick, not five (C-HE-14).
816	
817	**Variables:**
818	
819	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
820	|---|---|---|---|---|
821	| `T_now`, `T_run` | int tick | — | Kernel | The presented tick and the tick of the most recent Horror run |
822	| `tick_alpha` | real | [0, 1] | Kernel | Fraction within the current tick |
823	| `pos_prev`, `pos_curr` | int px | — | `horror.view` | Positions at the previous and the latest run |
824	
825	**Output Range:** `alpha5` in [0, 1]. **Example:** two ticks after the run with `tick_alpha` 0.5: `alpha5 = (2 + 0.5) / 5 = 0.5`, the draw position is the midpoint. A rig pose change on any tick that is not a multiple of 5 fails the cadence criterion.
826	
827	**Registry candidate:** none (render-side; owed to the Pipeline).

829	## Edge Cases
830	
831	Each case states the exact outcome and the rule it follows. Ids are `E-HE-n`. "Fizzle" always means the HE-17 outcome: RETREAT with no harm, no hairlines, no GOUGE or RUPTURE and no cooldown consumed, an already-laid touch-down smear stays (a fizzle before the hold stage lays none), the `"horror.tell"` draw stays consumed. Where a case settles something the Detailed Design left silent, it is marked *(orchestrator ruling)* and is repeated in the review questions. Cases that depend on an undesigned neighbour are marked *(provisional — <dep>)*.
832	
833	#### Zero, maximum and out-of-range values
834	
835	- **If a seat stands at exactly `R_SNAP_PX` (72 px) from P at resolution (E-HE-1)**: it is not hit. The disc is strict, `dx² + dy² < R_SNAP_PX²` with integers (`5184 < 5184` is false). The walk-out arithmetic of HE-F5 depends on the strictness, and an integer comparison keeps the outcome identical on replay.
836	- **If a seat that is already CRITICAL (integrity 3600) is struck (E-HE-2)**: `I = max(0, 3600 − 3200) = 400`, below `SUIT_HP_FAIL`, so FAILED → DOWNED → `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` → DEAD on Suit's ladder. The horror enters RETREAT after the hold. With no living, non-DOWNED candidate left, the target is the anchor (HE-13, HE-F8). At `cooldown_until_T` in BREACH it STALKs toward the anchor and runs anchor REACHes (hairlines and at most one GOUGE under `GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX`, never RUPTURE or `apply_suit_damage`, HE-16 (3)) until SUBSIDING sends it to RETREAT. It never LURKs in BREACH (phase view). The ladder and the death are Suit's, the restore is Save/Load's (HE-18).
837	- **If `apply_suit_damage` would take integrity below 0 (a patched suit at 2800 struck again) (E-HE-3)**: integrity clamps at 0 (`I_k = max(0, …)`, HE-F3); the mutator is Class B, clamp-never-reject, so Horror never sees a rejection and has no error path to write.
838	- **If the type row has `UNFOLD_LO` or `UNFOLD_HI` that is not a multiple of 5, `UNFOLD_HI < UNFOLD_LO`, or `UNFOLD_LO` below the HE-F5 bound (E-HE-4)**: the data load fails with a lint error and the type row is refused; nothing rounds silently. A silent round-up would bias every telegraph by 1 to 4 ticks at the exact bound that sizes the walk-out.
839	- **If `STRIKE_BP` is outside 3001..3500, `SUIT_PATCH_CAP_BP − STRIKE_BP` is below `SUIT_HP_FAIL`, or `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS` is at or below `STAGGER_TICKS` (E-HE-5)**: the data load fails the registered bounds (HE-F3, the third being the one-strike-never-kills-a-patched-suit bound) or the cooldown invariant (HE-F15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. A value outside the interval changes the hits-to-FAILED count, which is Suit's rung design, not Horror's to retune.
840	- **If a seat walks into the horror's mouth during a BREACH and the lit seat is already within `REACH_RANGE_PX` at the run the cooldown is clear (E-HE-6)**: the REACH begins on that run (conditions (a) to (f) of HE-14 hold); the telegraph is still at least `UNFOLD_LO` ticks and P is the seat's foot point at lock. A close approach shortens the horror's walk, never its warning.
841	- **If no waypoint is at least `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` from every living seat (a small body, seats on all sides) (E-HE-7)**: the horror holds its position and does nothing (the cornered rule of HE-11); it deposits no harm and lays no marks while still. A cornered horror is a stationary hazard, never a pursuer.
842	- **If a ring insert finds no SMEAR to evict (E-HE-8)**: unreachable by construction, because the per-kind quotas (HE-30) leave at least `MAX_MARKS − n_other_max` = 19 ring slots to SMEAR; a fixture that forces it fires the defensive assertion, which evicts the lowest `mark_id` of any kind and increments `horror_ring_invariant`, a defect signal and never a gameplay state *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
843	- **If more than `MARKS_PER_RUN_MAX` marks would be inserted in one run (E-HE-9)**: the first `MARKS_PER_RUN_MAX` are inserted in the order STRUCK, HAIRLINES, RIME, SMEAR and the rest are dropped and counted `horror_marks_withheld`. A run can legitimately want three (an ingress with smear, rime and hairlines); the cap bounds the dirty keys per tick (`MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256).
844	
845	#### Simultaneous rules
846	
847	- **If the predicate flips false between REACH begin and REACH end (the seat pod-hops, the breach is cleared early, the phase returns to CALM) (E-HE-10)**: the REACH fizzles at its last tick. The tip rested on P for the whole telegraph, a touch-down smear laid at the hold stage is a true mark and stays (a fizzle before the hold stage laid none), and the cooldown is not consumed, so a fizzle cannot starve the next legitimate REACH (HE-17).
848	- **If `reach_end_T` falls in SUBSIDING and the seat's section is still in `locus_body` (E-HE-11)**: the REACH resolves; the predicate holds in SUBSIDING for sections in `locus_body`, so `tell_window_contract` passes; the state then goes RETREAT. With `SUBSIDE_CANCELS_REACH` 1 it fizzles instead (the merciful variant, off by default; C-HE-10).
849	- **If a STRIKE is eligible for both GOUGE and RUPTURE on the same segment (E-HE-12)**: one hull deposit per STRIKE; RUPTURE when `rupture_ok` (which now requires an empty hit list), else GOUGE (HE-F17). The scrape (GOUGE) is always a separate, earlier, told act than the tear *(orchestrator ruling: HE-16 is silent on the tie)*.
850	- **If a REACH resolves on a seat that is already CRITICAL and staggered, beside a gouged hull face (E-HE-56)**: the seat is in the disc, so the hit list is not empty, `rupture_ok` is false and the deposit is a GOUGE (or none, if `GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX` is spent); the strike's `apply_suit_damage` takes the seat from 3600 to 400 and FAILED as in E-HE-2, and no breach opens beside the dying seat. The compound "CRITICAL, staggered, plus a hull rupture" is excluded by construction. If the same seat is outside the disc, a RUPTURE may be issued and the Graph raises its own told breach clock (RUPTURE sets the segment to `RUPTURE_HP` 3600: decompression takes about 131 s at the initial hole, LSG:707), which a CRITICAL walk-only seat (`V_WALK` 2, about 15 000 px in that time) can outwalk or patch; AC-HE-133 asserts both halves *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The miss-only RUPTURE rule is a user ruling (Open Question 2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
851	- **If one run wants a RUPTURE, a GOUGE and a CHILL while the window already holds 6 accepted calls (E-HE-13)**: the priority RUPTURE, GOUGE, CHILL applies within `MAX_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN`, then the window budget of 8 binds; RUPTURE and GOUGE are issued (window total 8), the CHILL is withheld (its rime mark is still laid) and `horror_footprints_withheld` increments. Harm outranks bookkeeping.
852	- **If a weld or cut changes the layout on the same tick a REACH resolves (E-HE-14)**: the locked P stays the stored integer; the same-room test (HE-15) and the closed-leaf test (HE-19) are re-evaluated against the layout as it is at resolution. A seat whose room now differs from P's room is not hit, so a layout change can only spare a seat, never reach one through a new wall.
853	- **If TELL ends in an abort on the same run a TRANSIT arrival completes, or at any earlier run while the record is outbound (E-HE-15)**: the abort is evaluated before the arrival (guard 5 precedes the TRANSIT exit), so the arrival is **cancelled**: no E6, no body in the player's ship, no new mark; the record heads back to `from_body_id` (the home body with `RETURN_HOME` 1) after `RETURN_DELAY_TICKS`, and an ingress mark already laid stays (HE-20). No strike, no mark burst *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; the earlier text had the record arrive as LURK, which injected a CALM presence and marks into the ship that had just held its fire)*.
854	- **If a second TELL begins while the record is in RETREAT from the previous breach (E-HE-16)**: RETREAT → LURK → STALK on the new `tell_epoch`; it never skips LURK, and the per-epoch counters (`strikes_epoch`, `gouges_epoch`, `ruptures_epoch`, `chill_epoch_dj`, `chill_deposits_epoch`) reset at the first run that sees the new `tell_epoch` (lazy reset, transition guard 2), and `gouged_seg_ids` empties with them *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
855	- **If Attention's phase changes on a tick on which `horror.step` does not run (E-HE-17)**: Horror reads the view as committed by Attention's most recent run and acts at its next run, at most 4 ticks later (HE-4). A REACH can therefore begin up to 4 ticks after BREACH entry plus the approach; the delay only ever lengthens the warning.
856	- **If a seat is STAGGERED during a REACH (E-HE-18)**: the Controller freezes it and ignores input for `STAGGER_TICKS` 30 (PCI:170; STAGGERED is not the CRITICAL walk-only cap). A seat staggered at REACH start whose walk command is issued at tick 54 still clears at 90 (91 on a diagonal octant) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: HE-F5 tick-indexing convention, G4)*. A seat staggered mid-walk loses the frozen ticks plus a re-command, and clears only on draws long enough to absorb them. Horror does not adapt (no stored state). The stagger is itself Suit's or the Controller's told consequence (another axis reaching CRITICAL, or friendly harm). A strike-two stagger cannot overlap the next REACH because `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS` 300 > `STAGGER_TICKS`.
857	
858	#### Degenerate strategies
859	
860	- **If a seat closes a door leaf between itself and the horror (E-HE-19)**: the leaf is solid to the horror (`solid_in`), it opens no door, and the straight segment from its foot point to P must not cross a closed leaf (HE-19), so no strike lands through it. Counterplay by design (HE-26); the price is the task and the ship under STRESS.
861	- **If the highest-`lux_pm` seat is in a room with no open route from the horror (E-HE-20)**: HE-13 still names that seat the target. The goal room is chosen over the full adjacency (closed leaves counted for distance), the movement uses the open-leaf graph, and the horror stops in the last reachable room at the closed leaf and begins no REACH (HE-14 condition (f) fails: `connected(horror foot, P)` is false across a closed leaf, and the distance test (d) alone would not stop it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier text cited a "segment test" that was not among conditions (a) to (e))*. It does not switch to a reachable but dimmer seat, because that would be a stored preference *(orchestrator ruling: HE-25 is silent on an unreachable target)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **It camps at the sill:** on the run it first becomes stationary there it lays one HAIRLINES mark on the leaf face (`held_at_leaf`, HE-26; no M17 call, no hull damage) and stays while that seat is the target and the phase is BREACH; the door is a visible, priced refuge, not a free one (delegated ruling G2, Open Question 33). A sealed seat is immune to the body; the Graph's own clocks and Attention's STRESS keep running. The share of told breaches with zero harm to a seat that stayed in the locus body is a playtest metric (30 to 60 % is the band; above 60 %, hull and ship consequences rise before any harm number does).
862	- **If the seat goes dark and stands still (E-HE-21)**: the target is the anchor on the next run (HE-13). The anchor REACH lays hairlines and, by default, one hull GOUGE under `GOUGES_PER_EPOCH_MAX` (HE-16 (3)); it never calls `apply_suit_damage` and never issues RUPTURE. Going dark spares the body and costs the ship, and every lit-only channelled verb is unavailable for the breach and the subside (about `BREACH_MIN_TICKS` + `SUBSIDE_TICKS` = 2100 ticks, 35 s). The anchor must lie within `HULL_CONTACT_PX` of a hull face for the GOUGE; if it does not, hairlines only.
863	- **If a dark seat stands within `R_SNAP_PX` of the anchor point at an anchor REACH's resolution (E-HE-22)**: no `apply_suit_damage` (an anchor REACH never harms a body, HE-16 (3)); the limb rests beside the seat and the hull takes the GOUGE. The seat has not been hunted, but a limb on its boots is not a safe place; whether a dark seat parked on the anchor should become targetable is an Open Question (the game-designer's `TOUCH_PX` guard was not adopted).
864	- **If the seat switches its lamp off after a REACH has begun (E-HE-23)**: P is already locked and stored; the strike resolves at P and hits every living seat in the disc, whether or not it was the target (HE-15). The lamp-off only changes the *next* run's target; nothing is remembered. Flapping the lamp to steer the horror costs the player the re-approach and cannot move a locked point.
865	- **If a seat stands in a thrown Chemlight pool (E-HE-24)**: the pool lights the seat, its `lux_pm` reaches `LIT_ON_PM` (a fresh Chemlight pool reads 700, so a seat standing in it is lit even with its own lamp off), and the seat is a candidate like any lit seat (HE-F8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The pool is never itself a target (a pool is not a seat). The glowstick works as a *work-light*: light the job, then step out of the pool dark; it does not pull the horror (HE-26).
866	- **If a seat walks through the horror (no collision) (E-HE-25)**: nothing happens in CALM, TELL or between REACHes; a rooted horror in REACH can be walked through, which may be an escape route out of a dead end. Accepted as a playtest item (Body's BDY-17: actors do not collide; the draw order decides how the overlap reads).
867	- **If a seat is in a dead-end room whose floor span is below `2 × R_SNAP_PX` (144 px) with a single exit (E-HE-26)**: it can be struck without a legal walk-out. This is an authoring defect, not a Horror rule: Derelict Authoring owes a lint (no dead-end room with floor span below 144 px and a single exit) and DA-29's wording note; Horror does not special-case it.
868	- **If a seat carries a module and a REACH begins (E-HE-27)**: the carrier needs 72 ticks (73 diagonal) against 40 available and is caught unless it drops the cargo within the reaction budget or `UNFOLD_TICKS ≥ 130` (11 of 18 draws), so a carrier who keeps the cargo is struck on 7 of 18 draws (38.9 %). Intended: hauling is where the horror bites and **dropping the cargo is the counterplay** (HE-24, C-HE-8); if the drop returns `OBSTRUCTED` (no free cell) the carrier is caught like a stationary seat, a lint case for Derelict Authoring and a question to Interaction (Open Question 7); the intended-price framing is a user ruling and the ruled lever is `R_SNAP_PX` 48 (HE-F5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
869	- **If a seat uses a tool on the horror, including a `tool_suppressant` placed by a test or debug fixture (E-HE-28; the item is not in the MVP start kit, user ruling X6)**: the verb fails `INVALID_TARGET` (IA-39); the item has no effect at MVP (AT-19) and `repel(origin, T)` is never called; the horror's state does not change; nothing is rewarded and nothing drops. Its acceptance criteria read NOT ASSESSED, never PASS (HE-39). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
870	
871	#### Layout, weld and cut
872

896	- **If `register_subject` (E6) returns false on a first registration (not a duplicate) (E-HE-44)**: the subject reads dark (`lux` 0, `lit` false); that is a **budget defect**, a failing criterion and a lint, never a gameplay state. "Fixture" means a deterministic scripted scenario with a fixed `world_seed`. A criterion that depends on an undesigned or in-flight neighbour is marked *(provisional — <dep>)* and reads **NOT ASSESSED** until that GDD exists, never PASS.

Logic and Integration rows are BLOCKING. Visual/Feel and UI rows are BLOCKING and require a **retained screenshot** under `production/qa/evidence/horror-entities/<ac-id>/` (a parse check is not a run), captured at **k = 1, `k_auto` and `k_auto + 2`** unless the row says otherwise, with a lead sign-off line (art-director for visuals, game-designer for feel). I'm cross-checking the timing conditions in AC-HE-125 and AC-HE-44 against the HE-F9 requirement that arrival time be at least the fallback time plus the 600-tick mark lead, noting that this 600 is relative to TELL entry and the run can shift up to 4 ticks later when unpinned.

Given Attention's tell_enter time is a multiple of 6, I'm computing Horror's first run after a 600-tick offset lands 4 ticks past the nominal BREACH entry, which means BREACH could be entered with ingress still pending for the shortest tells — a cry-wolf defect under E-HE-33 that would fail AC-HE-44's fixture. I'm also questioning whether the earlier 6-tick vs 5-tick grid misalignment was ever actually resolved, since the 600 = TELL_MIN relation leaves no slack at the placeholders.

Since an unpinned fixture with pending ingress fails the build, I should flag a recommendation: adjust the relation to include the run-alignment slack, like sum + (HORROR_RUN_TICKS − 1) ≤ TELL_MIN_TICKS, and pick a STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR_TICKS value that's a clean multiple of 5 to satisfy it.

Checking through the remaining acceptance criteria one by one, I'm verifying the retry delays, breach-clearing tolerances, co-op seat rules, and the modifier floor/strength bounds all stay consistent across their ranges — most look fine, though a few edge cases around pending ingress at the hull anchor and far-from-seat rooms need the recommended fix noted above.

1069	
1070	*Consulted: art-director (the visual half below follows its specification, reconciled with the rulings and the checkpoint rulings). Audio: Adaptive Audio & Tells is designed (`adaptive-audio-and-tells.md`) and owns every sound, mix and cue name, so this section states only the **facts Horror publishes** and the **mood the sound must sit inside**; every sound, layer, mix and cue name is Adaptive Audio's (HE-37; Designed, `adaptive-audio-and-tells.md`). Requirements, never pixels, shaders or code: implementation patterns are marked "-> ADR candidate". Constants named here that are not in the Tuning Knobs table are **presentation-side** (render only, never in `horror.state`, never hashed) and are listed in their own table below.*
1071	
1072	**Verdict.** Horror's visual job is narrow and the art bible already frames it (ART 5.4): a real horror is **a lit Void Steel mass with a thin iridescence band, seen only in someone's light, hidden by walls and by darkness, casting nothing, emitting nothing, and leaving honest web-grammar marks.** Everything else the player sees "from the horror" belongs to a neighbour (Attention's strands and tell, Failure & Trail's seam descriptors, Suit's rung and seam jet, Lighting's executed dips). Five decisions carry the section: (1) the rig body has **no contour, no shadow, no glow, binary alpha, and is never a flat fill**, so it cannot be mistaken for the stage-2 "shadow with no occluder" lie; (2) the REACH telegraph is the **limb-enters-the-cone-before-the-body** image with a **stationary tip on the locked strike point**, so the picture is itself the honest warning; (3) three marks ship (smear, branching rime, radial hairlines), each in a different value and topology class from every Failure & Trail trail, with the rime needing a **new palette entry** (C-HE-21); (4) every Horror visual is **truth channel**, the only corruptible things being the per-viewer omission of the body (Filter, Vertical Slice) and any phantom or class (c) rig the Filter drives, which **must leak violet or flesh and are never Horror's**; (5) the HUD shows **nothing** about a horror.

1132	- **VA-2 (reach cap).** The limb's maximum visual reach from the core is `3 × H_crew` = 3 × 53 = 159 base px (ART 5.4 and 8.2), so `REACH_RANGE_PX <= 159` (HE-F14).
1133	- **VA-3 (the strike zone is legible without a decal).** With the tip on the locked point, the player sees "this tile and one around it"; nothing draws the 72 px radius.
1134	- **VA-4 (stillness is the cue).** The telegraph depends on motion (unfold), then stillness (hold), then a one-step snap, and survives achromatopsia (shape and motion only) and reduced motion.
1135	- **VA-5 (minimum tip).** The limb tip is at least 4 base px wide (above the 2 × 2 floor), so an extended limb resolves at 1:1 at k = 1. At 384 × 216 the 80 px rig is about 37 % of field height and a 159 px reach is 74 % of field width; at k = 1 on 1080p it is 7.4 % of field height and only the form class (limb extended or not) is guaranteed.
1136	
1137	**Creep, unfold, snap (ART 5.4, 3.3).** *Creep* (LURK, STALK, RETREAT): continuous core displacement, stepped limb poses, no two consecutive steps repeat a limb configuration (hash on `(entity_id, pose_index)`), never a visible period. *Unfold* (REACH): the root-to-tip ripple above, no bounce and no overshoot (overshoot is the HUD *settle* word, ART 7.3). *Snap* (STRIKE): one pose step, the only fast motion Horror owns; the contrast with creep makes it readable; no afterimage, no trail. **Never:** squash and stretch, overshoot, a wind-up frame separate from the unfold, blur, motion lines.
1138	
1139	**Three "something at the edge of my light" sources, separated.**
1140	
1141	| Source | Owner | Where | Sync | The test the player already uses (AT:1184) |
1142	|---|---|---|---|---|
1143	| Tell strands, dust impulse, lamp gutter | Attention + Lighting | every lit region | **same beat, global** | "everywhere on the beat?" |
1144	| Horror L3 dip | Horror state, Lighting executes | lamps within `L3_RADIUS_PX` of **one horror** | **unsynchronised, local**, irregular | "one place, moving along a path?" |
1145	| Horror marks | Horror | one location per mark | none; persisted | "was it here before I arrived?" |
1146	| Sanity violet fringe | Sanity | the viewer's own rim | per viewer, breathing | "does my crewmate see it?" |

1148	L3 outranks L2 on a given lamp while active (LO-18), so the lamp nearest the horror shows the horror's rhythm and the rest of the room shows the beat. That is intended and is the test above (AC-HE-111); do not equalise them.
1149	
1150	**Lighting interaction (physical honesty).** A real horror contributes **no occluder, casts no shadow, emits nothing and changes no `lux`** (HE-2; EM-20 (c); LO rail 10). The beam passes through its volume and lights what is behind it; the rig's sprite hides what stands behind it by Y-sort only, exactly as crewmates do, so a horror is not singled out as a "ghost". The mitigation for the "solid thing that casts nothing" feel is that the rig is **normal-mapped and specular** (relief reacts to beam direction), never flat. Fiction gloss for the player-facing codex (creative-director, owed to the art bible): *"The web does not stop light; it only takes it. Nothing that belongs to the web casts a shadow, so a shadow with no occluder is never the web: it is you."*

The **iridescence band** is a thin-film specular band cycling teal, green, bronze and gold at low saturation, a band not a fill, the 270 to 330 degree arc excluded, peak at or under `BAND_PEAK_LSTAR_MAX` (about L\* 61, Attention's spike-confirmed ceiling at AT:1264: cited, never restated as Horror's, and not a registry name), no bloom at `glow_hdr_threshold`, intensity scaling with ring (faint at the outer ring, ART 4.3). **At MVP the horror lives in a ring-1 derelict, so the band is faint and the rig must read by silhouette and relief first.** **No contour** (D-AD2): a 1 px Void Steel contour on a Void Steel mass is invisible and ART 3.5 denies the web a hero shape, so the edge is defined by relief and the band. **Never flat:** a real mass shows relief highlights on its beam-facing sides (flip test, ART 6.2 rule 6); that is what separates it in a single still frame from the stage-2 lie, which is a flat violet-black polygon with no relief and no band (ART 4.4, 8.11 flag 2). **Unlit: not drawn**; the ambient-floor tint of ART 8.11 flag 1 applies to hull geometry and never to horrors.

Horror marks follow the **web rule**: ART 5.5 says "iridescent where lit", Principle 1 says a footprint should cost the player light to read, and a hull-tinted dark mark would sit between Failure & Trail's trails and Horror's marks and invite the collision AC-79 exists to separate. In the dark the player walks over unseen marks; that is the intended price.

1180	|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Against **Coolant Ice** (L\* 91) frost fans: a gap of 17 plus topology (a static radial fan at a fitting against an irregular fork away from fittings); this is the AC-79 collision fixture and value is a second separating axis. Against the **Chemlight pool** (L\* about 70): a **new greyscale collision**, separated by shape (a floor mark of fixed extent with branching edges against an omnidirectional pool around a thrown source sprite, steady then waning); a new ART 4.7 row is owed. This is an art-bible decision (creative-director, art-director); it blocks asset-spec for rime and hairlines, not this GDD. The fallback is to read FT:1427 as a rendered-appearance range and use Hull Grey, which then needs a "thin-element only" exemption for a floor mark (worse).

1213	### Audio: facts and mood
1214	
1215	Horror publishes **facts** (the table above) and owns no sound, mix or cue name. The mood any sound must sit inside is **patient, wet and structural**: closer to weather with intent than to a monster with a personality; it never roars at the camera. Constraints that bind Adaptive Audio and that Horror's lints assert (Audio AA-6 (the identity table), Sanity R28): the Horror sub-tell family is **disjoint** from Attention's tell family, the Graph loop sounds and Sanity's hallucination family; phantom horrors use the Filter and Sanity classes, **never the Graph witness acoustic classes**; Horror never mutes, ducks or filters anything; there is **no non-diegetic proximity cue** (a distance-scaled stinger is a meter by ear, Pillar 3); the source of every Horror sound is positional (the entity's `pos_px`, the segment, or `locked_pt`). The cues Horror's facts allow Audio to schedule, Designed (`adaptive-audio-and-tells.md`, AA-28): a floor-borne creep (V1, V2, V7), which Audio plays only while the entity is moving in LURK, STALK or RETREAT and never in TRANSIT; a REACH cue from `locked_pt`, a non-percussive lead-in started `REACH_RESOLVE_PRE_TICKS` 90 before `reach_end_T` and ending there with no impact transient (V3); a strike cue at `strike_T` (V6); a hull creak at an ingress or egress segment (V8, V9), which covers the transit (Audio AA-28 a, d). Marks and L3 dips are silent (Lighting's electrical grammar covers a dipping lamp).

Reduced motion cuts the idle sway to 0, the creep irregularity amplitude to one 15-degree quantum on one limb per pose step, and the L3 dip depth to `min(strength_pm, L3_STRENGTH_RM_CAP_PM)` (cap 150 permille, so the L3 factor is at least 850; the earlier "`MOD_FLOOR_PM`-bound minimum" was ambiguous between a depth and a remaining factor), but **never** the unfold-hold-snap sequence *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. 1251	- **Low vision.** The ambient-floor option reveals hull only, **never** horrors or marks (web rule): the horror stays beam-dependent.
1252	- **Deaf and hard of hearing.** The visual channels are the picture-telegraph, L3 dips and marks. The telegraph is beam-dependent only for the limb **body**; its tip rests on the victim's own foot point inside the victim's own light (HE-14), so the tip is lit for the victim (R-2, resolved by CP-1). Audio's facts are Audio's.

1255	- **Zoom (ladder k in [1, k_auto + 2]).** All Horror lengths are base px and scale with `s = field_h / 360`. Marks follow FT-34: full legibility at `k_auto` and the first zoom-out; at k = 1 only polarity, form class and value class are guaranteed, so a hairline may not resolve (accepted and logged, not a licence to cull marks).

1286	## Game Feel
1287	
1288	Horror has **no input of its own**: the player never presses anything at it (PC-12, HE-38). Its "feel" is the feel of being *read* by something patient and then *choosing* inside a window the design guarantees is long enough. The targets below therefore specify the **input-to-feedback chain** (what the player does in answer to what the horror shows), the **timing of the picture** (ticks, pose counts, px) and the **absence of every action-game punctuation** (hit-stop, shake, flash), each as a number. Conversions: 1 tick = 16.7 ms at `TICK_RATE` 60; one Horror run = 5 ticks = 83.3 ms = one 12 fps rig pose; 95 ticks = 1.58 s; 180 ticks = 3.00 s; 300 ticks = 5.00 s. Every number is `[PLACEHOLDER]` pending the blind-legibility playtest (AC-HE-106) and cites its Tuning Knob or Formula.
1289	
1290	### Feel Reference
1291	
1292	- **Adopt: the fixed-point telegraph of boss-style area attacks (Souls-like ground strikes, platformer stomps).** A long, readable wind-up whose *area is locked at its start*, so that moving out always works and a hit is the player's own stillness. Borrowed quality: **committed, heavy, fair.** The horror's snap is the only fast thing in its vocabulary, and it lands on a place the player was shown for one to three seconds (HE-14, HE-F5).
1293	- **Adopt: *Alien: Isolation*'s one persistent, physically present body** (a true position, never despawned) **and *Darkwood*'s light that attracts and marks that carry the past** (HE-13, HE-30). Borrowed quality: weather with intent, not a monster with a personality.
1294	- **Adopt in spirit: *Project Zomboid*'s "death is final and common"** (the user's decision), bounded to three told strikes; and *Amnesia*'s "you cannot fight it, only hide" (no attack input).
1295	- **Anti-reference (reject precisely):** *Alien: Isolation*'s director-driven menace gauge and grab-instakill (a hidden number and an unreadable death); any action-game hit-stop, screen shake, damage number or red flash (HE-38, the camera refuses horror callers); a stinger that scales with distance (a meter by ear, Pillar 3). **It must not feel** like a jump-scare machine, a boss with a health bar, or a creature that "locks on" and follows you (validation target 4).
1296	
1297	### Input Responsiveness
1298	
1299	The only inputs in the chain belong to the player (walk, lamp, door, pod) and to the sim (the horror's run). The budget is the **walk-out window** of HE-F5: from the limb entering the cone to the seat standing on the disc boundary, the player gets `UNFOLD_LO` 95 ticks, of which 54 are the assumed reaction allowance, 1 the kernel's command application and 37 the walk on the slowest (diagonal) octant (`t_out_max(V_WALK)`, HE-F2; 36 on a cardinal octant), leaving **3 ticks (50 ms) of slack** at the shortest draw (4 on a cardinal octant), which is also the whole allowance for input and display latency (`INPUT_LATENCY_TICKS`, unmeasured, HE-F5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
1300	
1301	| Action or cause | Max latency to visible or audible response | Frame budget (60 fps) | Notes |
1302	|---|---|---|---|
1303	| Attention's phase edge on a non-run tick to Horror acting on it | 4 ticks (67 ms) | 4 | Horror reads `attention.view` as committed by Attention's last run and acts at its next run (HE-4, E-HE-17); it only ever *lengthens* the warning |
1304	| Horror state change (REACH begin, STRIKE, RETREAT) to the rig pose on screen | 1 tick (17 ms) after the run that made it | 1 | The pose is a function of `(state, state_enter_T, now)`; the run that commits `locked_pt` and `reach_end_T` is the run whose pose the presenter draws |
1305	| Player's walk command to the seat moving | 1 tick (17 ms) | 1 | Kernel command application at `apply_tick >= T + 1` (KRN D.4); counted inside the 95-tick budget |
1306	| Player switches the lamp off to the horror's *next-run* target changing | 5 ticks (83 ms) | 5 | Target recomputed each run (HE-13); an **in-flight REACH is unaffected** (P is locked, E-HE-23) |
1307	| `strike_T` to the positional strike cue starting | 1 tick (17 ms) | 1 | A requirement on Adaptive Audio (Designed, `adaptive-audio-and-tells.md`, AA-28 c); the cue is the witness of strike one (HE-15) |
1308	| Strike to Suit's rung change and the Controller's stagger | at the next `suit.vitals` run, at most 6 ticks (100 ms) after the hit, with no hold (SE-23, `SUIT_EXO_BYPASS_LIMITER` 1); the Controller's stagger follows on the cap falling edge it reads after `suit.vitals` (PC-9) | <= 6 | Suit's and the Controller's; stagger lasts `STAGGER_TICKS` 30 (500 ms) |
1309	| Closing a door leaf to the strike no longer reaching through it | the same tick | 0 | The room test and the closed-leaf test are evaluated at resolution (HE-19) |
1310	
1311	### Animation Feel Targets
1312	
1313	"Startup" is the telegraph before the act has any effect; "Active" is the committed window in which the act is fixed and nothing the player does changes where it lands; "Recovery" is the horror's committed, vulnerable-in-the-world time (it is never vulnerable to the player; recovery is the player's **breathing room**). One pose = 5 ticks. All counts follow `UNFOLD_TICKS` in [95, 180] (19 to 36 poses).
1314	
1315	| Animation | Startup (ticks, poses) | Active (ticks, poses) | Recovery (ticks, poses) | Feel goal | Notes |
1316	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
1317	| **REACH** (enter + unfold + hold) | enter ~15 %: 15 to 27 (3 to 5); unfold ~55 %: 50 to 100 (10 to 20) | hold ~30 %, never under 30 ticks: 30 to 54 (6 to 11); **the tip does not move** | resolves into the snap | Committed, deliberate, readable: a heavy thing placing a limb | The limb enters the cone before the body; no icon, ring or decal; `reach_a/b/c` poses (V3, V4) |
1318	| **STRIKE** (snap) | 0 (no wind-up beyond the unfold) | 1 pose = 5 ticks (83 ms), then held for `STRIKE_HOLD_RUNS` 2 = 10 ticks (167 ms) | RETREAT begins at the end of the hold | Crisp and binary: the only fast motion Horror owns | No lunge travel, afterimage or trail (HE-24); the touch-down smear and the positional cue are the punctuation |
1319	| **REACH fizzle** | n/a | the reverse of the unfold poses over the same stage lengths | none; the cooldown is not consumed | Identical to a deliberate withdrawal, so a harmless hold cannot be told from a harmful one | The hold itself is always honest (V5) |
1320	| **RETREAT** | 0 | creep at `V_CREEP_MPX` 1000: 5 px per run; 96 ticks out to a nominal waypoint at 192 px | `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS` 300 (5.0 s) before STALK may resume; 65 ticks back at `V_HUNT_MPX` | A retreat reads as a retreat, not a hover (`t_out` 96 is inside the cooldown, HE-F15) | The realised period of a seat that does not move is 460 to 545 ticks (7.7 to 9.1 s); the earliest next strike is 395 ticks (6.6 s) after the last |
1321	| **Creep** (LURK, STALK in a TELL) | n/a | 1 px per tick, a pose per run, hash-irregular limb choice, no repeated configuration in consecutive steps | n/a | Patient, wet, structural; never a metronome (not the tell's beat), never a jitter | Dwell 900 ticks (15 s) at a LURK waypoint |
1322	| **Hunt** (STALK in BREACH) | n/a | 1.5 px per tick on average (7 then 8 px per run); a walker gains 0.5 px per tick on it | n/a | Inevitable but outwalkable: pressure, not a chase | `V_HUNT_MPX` below `V_WALK × 1000` is the escape invariant (HE-F6) |
1323	| **Ingress** | the ingress mark is laid 60 ticks (1.0 s) before the body | the rig emerges across the wall footprint's south edge; alpha is 0 or 255 | n/a | A body crossing a light boundary, never a fade | At least 300 ticks (5.0 s) of published stalk remain before the shortest tell ends (HE-F9) |
1324	| **Mark lay-down** | 3 frames (smear, rime) or 2 (hairlines), 5 ticks each | hold on the last lay-down frame (stage 0) | aged frames at stage 1 from age 6000 ticks and stage 2 from age 12000 ticks (thirds of `MARK_LIFE_TICKS` 18000) | A floor that remembers, readable as wet, tacky, dry | Frame swaps on a binary-alpha sprite; no fade |
1325	
1326	### Impact Moments
1327	
1328	Every row is **0 by design** (HE-38, the anti-pillar "not a combat game"; the camera refuses a Horror-tagged caller). The punctuation the strike *does* carry is listed after the table. "Configurable?" is **No** for every row: these are lint failures, not tuning options.
1329	
1330	| Impact type | Duration | Effect | Configurable? |
1331	|---|---|---|---|
1332	| Hit-stop (freeze frames) | 0 ms | none | No (HE-38; AC-HE-72, AC-HE-116) |
1333	| Screen shake | 0 ms | none | No (PIPE C1, C9; the jolt API refuses a Horror-tagged caller) |
1334	| Camera impact or zoom punch | 0 ms | none | No (the camera never reacts to a horror) |
1335	| Hit flash, vignette, chromatic aberration | 0 ms | none | No (Visual/Audio: forbidden feedback) |
1336	| Damage number, health pip, threat bar | n/a | none | No (HE-38) |
1337	| Controller rumble | none from Horror | Neither the Player Controller & Input GDD nor Suit & Equipment defines a rumble rule; if one is added for the stagger or the CRITICAL rung it is theirs (HUD & Suit Layer: designed (`hud-and-suit-layer.md`)) | No (not Horror's) |
1338	| Time-scale slowdown | 0 ms | none | No |
1339	
1340	**The punctuation the strike does carry:** the single **snap pose** (5 ticks, then a 10-tick hold), the **touch-down smear** laid at the point 25 to 50 ticks earlier, at the start of the hold stage, and still on the floor, **Audio's positional cue** starting within 1 tick of `strike_T`, the **STRUCK burst** laid at P only when a seat was hit (a miss leaves the smear alone), and **Suit's own consequence** (the rung, the stagger, from strike two the seam jet). Strike one has no persistent witness on the body (Suit's STRAINED rung is inert by design, SE:83); the strike and the STRUCK mark on the floor are the witness, which is why those things exist (HE-15, C-HE-25).
1341	
1342	### Weight and Responsiveness Profile
1343	
1344	- **Weight.** Heavy and deliberate. The horror is slower than the walker (1.0 to 1.5 px per tick against 2), roots its body for the whole telegraph and resolves in one step. It never hurries, never poses and never roars.
1345	- **Player control.** High at every moment until the commit. The strike point is locked, so *moving out of the disc always works*; the player can course-correct for the whole telegraph and, because there is no tracking, cannot be "chased" into a hit. Control ends only for a carrier (`V_CARRY` 1 needs 72 ticks, 73 diagonal, against 40 available, so a carrier who keeps the cargo is struck on 7 of 18 draws; the answer is to drop the cargo) and for a seat that stands still.
1346	- **Snap quality.** The creep and unfold are stepped at 12 fps with smoothed position (analogue in motion, discrete in pose); the strike is a **binary one-step snap**. The contrast between the long stillness of the hold and the single step of the snap is the whole read.
1347	- **Acceleration model.** Simulation feel, no ramp: speed is a constant cadence (`v_eff` per tick from the accumulator, HE-F6), and a speed change at a phase edge is instantaneous in the sim and invisible as acceleration on screen (position is interpolated, pose is stepped). There is no lunge momentum and no overshoot.
1348	- **Failure texture.** Fair, never random: the player was shown the limb, the stillness and the smear, and a hit reads as "I stood there" or "I was carrying". The target is that **at least 80 % of horror-caused deaths are described with a cause the player saw** (validation target 1). There is nothing hidden: no stored aggro, no lock-on, no number. Dying is lethal (user decision), restores from the newest autosave, and shows no death screen or beat (SL-7).
1349	
1350	### Feel Acceptance Criteria
1351	
1352	Subjective targets stated precisely enough to get consistent verdicts; the manual rows that measure them are the numbered criteria in Acceptance Criteria Group M, and the sample rule (N >= 10) applies.
1353	
1354	- [ ] Playtesters describe the telegraph as "it was aiming at that spot" or equivalent for at least 87.5 % of first-time players (7 of 8 equivalent, N >= 10; AC-HE-106); none uses "cheap", "unfair" or "came out of nowhere" unprompted for a *told* strike.
1355	- [ ] Of the players who were hit, at least 75 % call it avoidable (AC-HE-106); at least 80 % of horror-caused deaths are described with a cause the player saw (AC-HE-116).
1356	- [ ] The unfold-hold-snap sequence reads at k = 1, `k_auto` and `k_auto + 2` as "limb extended, tip on a tile" (at k = 1 only "limb extended") (AC-HE-107).
1357	- [ ] The creep reads as patient and irregular: no tester says "glitchy", "teleporting", "jittery" or "puppet" (AC-HE-108, AC-HE-117); pose changes land only on multiples of 5 ticks.
1358	- [ ] No tester reports a hit-stop, shake, flash or number from the horror (AC-HE-116), and none reports an unfair pop-in on ingress (AC-HE-112).
1359	- [ ] A player who reacts within the 54-tick allowance escapes at every legal draw of `UNFOLD_TICKS` (AC-HE-88); the 3-tick slack (4 on a cardinal octant) is felt as "just made it" at the shortest draw, never as "it hit me where I was not" *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
1360	- [ ] Zero testers describe the horror "remembering" or "locking on" across a lamp-off (validation target 4, AC-HE-115).
1361	- [ ] The breathing gap between a snap and the next limb (at least 365 ticks, 6.1 s, for a seat that stays in range) is described as a lull to act in, not as a long pause or a screech (AC-HE-115).
1362	- [ ] Reduced motion keeps the telegraph readable (AC-HE-113).
1363	
1364	## UI Requirements
1365	
1366	**Horror Entities has no UI of its own.** It owns no HUD element, no instrument, no chart-table row, no menu and no overlay, and it must not acquire one: Pillar 3 says the web's attention and its consequences are "shown in the world, never a meter", and the anti-pillar against a combat game rules out every standard enemy-awareness widget. Everything the player learns about a horror comes through the world: the rig in the beam, the marks on the floor, the dips on nearby lamps, Audio's positional facts, and Suit's and Failure & Trail's consequences. The surfaces that exist in the game and touch this system are owned elsewhere; this section states what each must **not** do and what Horror supplies. A UX spec is therefore not requested for Horror; the UX note at the end is a *negative* requirement routed to the HUD owner.
1367	
1368	| Information | Display location | Update frequency | Condition | Owner |
1369	|---|---|---|---|---|
1370	| Where a horror is, what state it is in, which seat it prefers, where its limb will land | **Nowhere in the HUD.** The player reads the rig, the limb tip and the touch-down smear in the world | n/a | never | Horror (world only) |
1371	| That a hit landed | The snap pose, Audio's positional cue and, afterwards, the STRUCK burst on the floor at P (a miss leaves only the touch-down smear) (HE-15); then Suit's own rung display and stagger | on the strike | a seat in the disc | Suit & Equipment, HUD & Suit Layer |
1372	| Suit integrity after strikes | Suit's existing instrument or HUD row (STRAINED is inert and carries no witness by design, SE:83; CRITICAL shows the leak, seam jet and stagger) | Suit's | Suit's | Suit & Equipment, HUD & Suit Layer |
1373	| The ship's hull damage from a GOUGE or RUPTURE | Failure & Trail's hull descriptor and the Graph's own instruments | the Graph's | a hull act | Failure & Trail, In-World Instruments |
1374	| That the lamp is on or off (the horror's target rule) | Controller and Suit's lamp state; the lit-only verb gating | immediate | always | Player Controller, Interaction |
1375	| Where it has been | the marks themselves (smear, rime, hairlines), never a map pin, trail overlay or "last seen" marker on the Chart Table or Web Map | n/a | never | Horror (world only); Chart Table, Web Map must not add one |
1376	| True horror positions, target, state, locked point, budgets and counters | **Debug Overlay (True Values), development builds only** | per run | developer flag | Debug Overlay (`horror.view` is read-only); never exposed as an accessibility feature |
1377	| Save status | Save/Load's pause-panel and failed-write notice, unrelated to Horror | Save/Load's | Save/Load's | Save/Load |
1378	
1379	**Rules for the surfaces that exist (negative requirements, each an acceptance criterion).**
1380	- No HUD, instrument, chart-table or web-map element shows a horror, a threat bar, a proximity indicator, a direction, an off-screen arrow, a countdown to a strike, a "last seen" pin or a target ring, **under any accessibility setting** (Pillar 3, AT-24; AC-HE-119).
1381	- No audio-to-visual accessibility feature may name, point to or time a horror (a captioned cue such as "something nearby" is a proximity indicator by another name). The accessibility mapping for Horror's audio facts is an Open Question for the accessibility specialist and the HUD owner, with the constraint that it never reveals position, state or direction.
1382	- No cursor, reticle or interaction prompt appears on a horror: HORROR subjects take no verb and any forced command is `INVALID_TARGET` (IA-39, AC-IA-113).
1383	- The Debug Overlay's true-value drawing is a development tool; a shipping build cannot enable it.
1384	- Accessibility options that change Horror's presentation (reduced motion, reduced flashing, ambient-floor reveal) act on the world drawing described in Visual/Audio Requirements and never add a surface (the ambient-floor option reveals hull only, never a horror or a mark).
1385	
1386	**UX note (deliberately not a UX flag).** This system has **no UI of its own**, so no `/ux-design` pass is requested for it. The HUD & Suit Layer (designed (`hud-and-suit-layer.md`)), In-World Instruments, Chart Table and Debug Overlay (designed (`debug-overlay-true-values.md`)) UX specs must repeat the negative requirements above and list "no horror element" in their own acceptance criteria; the HUD state list in AC-HE-119 is finalised from the HUD UX spec. `(provisional — In-World Instruments and Chart Table UX specs)`.

**Output Range:** `leaf_w`, `gap` in `[0, 96]`; the product `width_px × area` is at most `96 × 128 = 12,288`. At `area = 0` the leaf covers the doorway; at `area = area_max` there is no rect. Because the formula has no threshold, a binary jump `0 ↔ area_max` is binary by consequence and `DOOR_LIGHT_OPEN_PM` is retired (LY-9).

**Example (`area_max` 64):** `area` 0 → `leaf_w` 96; 32 → 48; 64 → 0; 21 → `96 − floor_div(2016, 64) = 96 − 31 = 65`, `gap` 31; 10 → `gap` 15, 11 → `gap` 16. `area_pass_min(16) = ceil_div(1024, 96) = 11` (check: `gap(10) = 15 < 16`, `gap(11) = 16`) and `area_pass_min(8) = ceil_div(512, 96) = 6` (`gap(5) = 7`, `gap(6) = 9`). With `area_max` 128: `area_pass_min(16) = 22` (`gap(21) = 15`, `gap(22) = 16`) and `area_pass_min(8) = 11`. Leaf rect of `door_cryo_s` (E-W wall footprint `y` in `[384, 408)`, doorway `x` in `[240, 336)`, hinge `LOW`/west, `area_max` 64) at `area` 32: `[240, 288) × [384, 408)`, gap `[288, 336)`. **Close-safety:** closing from `area` 32 to 20 gives `leaf_w = 96 − floor_div(1920, 64) = 66`, leaf `[240, 306) × [384, 408)`; a foot box `[296, 312) × [384, 392)` overlaps it (`240 < 312`, `296 < 306`, `384 < 392`, `384 < 408`), so `leaf_would_overlap` is true and a PLAYER-origin close returns `OBSTRUCTED` (LY-11). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Mated-hatch example (the seam-straddling case):** the `fixture_airlock` weld of D.6 with `area_max` 64 (the minimum of 64 and 128): the opening's leaves are A's `[672, 696) × [240, 240 + leaf_w)` and B's `[696, 720) × [240, 240 + leaf_w)`. Closing from `area` 32 to 20 gives `leaf_w` 66, so both leaves reach `y` 306. The foot box `[696, 712) × [296, 304)` overlaps **only B's leaf** (`696 < 720`, `296 < 306`; against A's leaf `696 < 696` is false), so `leaf_would_overlap(opening, 20, [box])` is true; a check made against A's leaf alone would have returned false. (A box `[688, 704) × [296, 304)` straddling the seam overlaps both.) The (MVP) binary close tests the jump to `area` 0 the same way.

**Passage record (`door_passage`)** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: `orientation` = `EW` for a door in an E-W wall, `NS` in a N-S wall. For a doorway starting at `s` in an E-W wall whose footprint starts at `w`: `sill_rect = [s, s + 96) × [w, w + 24)`; `open_extent_px = gap(area)` (0 when closed, 96 when `area = area_max`); `gap_rect`, hinge `LOW` = `[s + leaf_w, s + 96) × [w, w + 24)`, hinge `HIGH` = `[s, s + gap) × [w, w + 24)`; a N-S wall swaps the axes (`sill_rect = [w, w + 24) × [s, s + 96)`). `gap_rect` is NONE iff `open_extent_px = 0`, and equals `sill_rect` when `area = area_max`. The OUT convention is LY-12 (b)'s: every returned rect is the occupied span `(x0, y0, x1 − 1, y1 − 1)` (the half-open figures above are the stored form). The read returns NO passable flag: the caller compares `open_extent_px` with its foot extent `F` (`passes(F) ⇔ gap ≥ F`; `F` supplied by Body/Controller, PCI:103: 16 across an E-W doorway, 8 across a N-S one). **Mated hatch:** the opening's single `area_max = min(a, b)` and the fixed LOW hinge (LY-9, LY-15) apply; each section answers for its OWN leaf in its OWN section-local frame, and both answer the same `open_extent_px`. The read re-uses the leaf value `layout.doors` last projected (the same `leaf_w` that sizes the leaf rect), so collision, light and passage cannot disagree and `opening()` is not read a second time; an unknown opening reads as closed (the existing `opening_unknown` edge case), so `open_extent_px = 0`. It changes exactly when `leaf_version(section_id)` bumps (LY-12 d), so a reader's cache keyed on `version(section_id)` is correct (Horror HE-25 keys so). Cost: O(1) integer arithmetic, no `QueryBuffer`, safe in a P3 hook after `layout.doors` (`body.integrate` is `after: [controller.step, layout.doors]` and `horror.step` follows `body.integrate`, so a Horror run sees same-tick state).

**Worked values** (`door_cryo_s`, E-W, `s` 240, `w` 384, hinge LOW, `area_max` 64; `sill_rect` span (240, 384, 335, 407) in every row): `area` 0 → `open_extent_px` 0, `gap_rect` NONE; `area` 4 → `gap` floor_div(384, 64) = 6, LOW (330, 384, 335, 407), HIGH (240, 384, 245, 407); `area` 8 → 12, LOW (324, 384, 335, 407), HIGH (240, 384, 251, 407); `area` 11 → floor_div(1056, 64) = 16, LOW (320, 384, 335, 407), HIGH (240, 384, 255, 407); `area` 32 → 48, LOW (288, 384, 335, 407), HIGH (240, 384, 287, 407); `area` 64 → 96, `gap_rect` (240, 384, 335, 407). **N-S variant** (a harness-added door, as AC-52 adds `door_b`; `w` 384, `s` 240, footprint `x` in [384, 408), doorway `y` in [240, 336)): `sill_rect` span (384, 240, 407, 335); `area` 8 (12 px): LOW (384, 324, 407, 335), HIGH (384, 240, 407, 251); `area` 4 (6 px): LOW (384, 330, 407, 335), HIGH (384, 240, 407, 245). | Query | Returns | Frame | Order | Valid after | Owner of the fact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `room_at(section_id, px) -> room_id \| NONE` (sill px → `sill_room`) | id | section-local | n/a | `restore`; hook-callable (Suit SE-3) | Layout |
| `compartment_of_room(room_id)`, `room_of_compartment(cid)` | id mapping via `comp_base` | n/a | n/a | `restore` | Layout (mapping); Graph (compartment) |
| `V(room_id)`, `exposed_tiles(room_id)` | ints | n/a | n/a | `restore` | Layout |
| `room_surface(compartment_id) -> {floor_tiles[], wall_faces[]}` | FT:306 shape | section-local | tile id ascending | `restore` | Layout |
| `room_boundary(room_id)` | polyline | section-local | clockwise from min tile | `restore` | Layout |
| `floor_tile_at(section_id, px)` | tile or `NONE` | section-local | n/a | `restore` | Layout |
| `anchor_geometry(anchor)`, `subject_anchors(section_id)` | LY-23 | section-local | `local_key` ascending | `restore` | Layout |
| `occluder_source(body_id)` → `rects_in(aabb, out)`, `version(section_id)`, `static_version(section_id)`, `leaf_version(section_id)` | records into the caller's `QueryBuffer`: `keys` (int64), occupied spans `(x0, y0, x1−1, y1−1)`, flags byte (LY-12 e); input `aabb` half-open | BODY | ascending key `(section_id, idx)` | `post_restore` (door leaves) | Layout *(Amended 2026
| `solid_in(body_id, aabb, out)` | SOLID records into the caller's `QueryBuffer`, **same layout and the same occupied-span output as `rects_in`**; input `aabb` half-open | BODY | ascending key | `post_restore` | Layout *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

| `leaf_would_overlap(opening_ref, area, foot_boxes[])` — `opening_ref` is the Graph OPENING `edge_id`; evaluates **every** leaf projected from it, on both sections of a mated hatch, and is true if any overlaps any foot box (LY-11); foot boxes half-open, body frame | bool | BODY | n/a | `post_restore` | Layout (foot boxes: caller) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `leaf_obstruction(opening_ref, area, foot_boxes[])` — the geometric "why" of a refused close (LY-11) | `{box_index, leaf_slot}` or `NONE` | BODY | first box in caller order | `post_restore` | Layout *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `socket_plan`, `can_attach`, `can_build`, `can_detach`, `can_discard` | plan / reason; the `can_attach` preview payload is `{reason, hatch_one_sided, openings_count}` (LY-14) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | n/a | lane order | `restore` | Layout |
| `section_offset(section_id)`, `body_of(section_id)`, `sections_of(body_id)` | ints | body | ascending | `restore` | Layout |

toolu_01FrzcW2Kvkwffu9TUxBqZN7.summary: Verdict for the fourth read-only pass of design/gdd/horror-entities.md: no BLOCKING defects; 15 RECOMMENDED and 2 NICE findings remain. The file is 512,619 bytes (1774 lines, 145 ACs). review-receipts.sh printed RECEIPT, CHANGED for the GDD and CHANGED for the registry; both changed since the last logged review, as expected after the 2026-10-28 cross-GDD fix pass. gdd-structure-check.sh reports PRESENT for all 8 required sections: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria. Every GDD named in Dependencies exists. Only Depth Rings & Scarcity, Knowledge Codex & Logs and Co-op have no file, and under R9 they stay provisional. Both prior blockers are RESOLVED, checked in this file and in Layout. (1) door_passage: Layout now publishes it (LY-28, D.5, AC-180) and HE-19/25 and AC-127/128 conform to its fields, formula and foot extents. (2) AC-HE-88 vs AC-HE-130: both now use HE-F5's convention, and I recomputed the a = 54 and a = 59 cases. I also recomputed the other numbers I spot-checked, and they hold. These were the Poisson table, the 324-pair enumeration, the 7-of-18 carrier figure, the mark-ring arithmetic, the L3 flash rate, the integrity ladder and bounds, the REACH timeline and the golden UNFOLD_TICKS lists. The recommended items fall into four groups. Cross-GDD naming and ownership: `threat_counter` exists only in this GDD while the kernel exports `rng_derive_epoch`, which also leaves AC-HE-136's NOT ASSESSED sentence stale; and the UNFOLD_SCALE_PCT command is specified with a HOST origin the kernel does not have. Unresolved carry-overs: the hold stage is defined two ways (25-50 ticks in the sim, 30-55 in the art and feel tables), the door-eject run can reach 9 solid_in queries against a cap of 5, AC-HE-17's hash is stale, the ingress fallback has no slack for the 5/6-tick grid, and a stale-text sweep is still owed. A gap the new door_passage exposed: no read pairs hatches across a welded seam, so welded-body pathing is undefined. Open items that R21 says should be decided: the Rime palette entry, the D_marks floor and the Suit patch-cap range floor. The registry's horror.state manifest is stale against HE-41. None of these makes implementation of slice 1 wrong or impossible, but items 1 and 2 should land before slice 1 starts because they gate it.

findings.section: HE-42, HE-14, HE-F5, AC-HE-24/80/136, OQ 29/31, Cross-References (carried over from the 2026-10-27 review)
findings.finding: `threat_counter(c)` is not published by the kernel. grep finds it only in horror-entities.md, in 20 places. The kernel (command-simulation-layer.md D.10, KRN-EPO-04), Attention (AC-AT-130) and the registry (`rng_derive_epoch`, and horror.state `rng`) all name the one derivation `rng_derive_epoch(world_seed, stream, rng_counter)`. HE-42 calls `threat_counter` 'the kernel's one derivation' and tells the reader to gate slice 1 on the kernel 'publishing threat_counter'. That gate cannot be met as written. Under G1 the owner's name wins. AC-HE-136 still ends 'read NOT ASSESSED until Save/Load and the kernel publish kernel.clock.restore_epoch and threat_counter', but both are already published: kernel.clock carries restore_epoch, Save/Load has slot_epoch.bin, SL-23 and AC-SL-145, and the kernel has KRN-EPO-04. A NOT ASSESSED row blocks story close. AC-HE-24 asserts the call to a function that does not exist, and the AC-HE-136 lint 'restore_epoch read only through threat_counter' cannot be written.
findings.fix: Replace `threat_counter(counter)` with `rng_derive_epoch(world_seed, "horror.tell", counter)` everywhere (HE-14, HE-42, HE-F5, E-HE-41, AC-HE-24/80/82/136, OQ 29/31, the Interactions and Dependencies rows, the knob-source table), and keep the formula c + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE x restore_epoch only as a citation of kernel D.10. Delete the NOT ASSESSED sentence of AC-HE-136 and re-point it at the closing stories KRN-EPO-04 and AC-SL-145. Then grep both spellings (G3).

findings.section: HE-F5 / Tuning Knobs (UNFOLD_SCALE_PCT, `horror_set_unfold_scale`) (carried over)
findings.finding: The accessibility lever is specified as 'a command with HOST origin'. The kernel's CR-6/CR-7 say allowed_origins is a subset of {PLAYER, SYSTEM}, and HOST is a kernel mode, not an origin. No sibling GDD defines `horror_set_unfold_scale` (grep finds it only here), and no settings, pause or HUD surface carries it. As written the command cannot be submitted, so the GDD's own fallback for a failed blind-legibility test ('UNFOLD_SCALE_PCT is the player-side answer', OQ 17) does not exist. HE-6/HE-28 also say Horror submits no SYSTEM command, so SYSTEM is not an option. Under G6 this is a GAP: the owner adds the surface.
findings.fix: Define it as a PLAYER-origin world-option command owned by Horror (CR-6 table: allowed_origins {PLAYER}, actor_binding NONE, range-checked 100..200, hashed in the replay log, applied at its apply_tick). Add one row to the Pause/Settings panel owner (HUD or Chart Table, no in-world indicator, AT-24). Add an AC that submits 99, 100, 150 and 201 and a SYSTEM-origin attempt, and asserts accept/reject and replay equality. Update HE-F5, HE-41 and the knob row.

findings.section: HE-14 / Visual-Audio 'telegraph as a picture' table and V4 / Game Feel Animation table / Gaps list (carried over)
findings.finding: The hold stage still has two definitions. The sim (HE-14: hold_start_T = reach_end_T - 5 x floor(3 x n/10)), AC-HE-143 and the Game Feel 'punctuation' paragraph give 25 to 50 ticks (5 to 10 poses). The Visual/Audio stage table says 'last ~30 %, 6 poses at the lower bound: 28.5 ticks rounded up to 30; 11 at the upper', Game Feel row REACH says 'hold ~30 %, never under 30 ticks: 30 to 54 (6 to 11)', and the Gaps list says 'not under 27 ticks ... 28.5 ticks, 6 poses'. The ring entry for the touch-down smear is laid by the sim at hold_start_T, but V4 says the smear is laid 'on the first pose step of this stage', so the presenter's hold pose and the true mark disagree by one pose at n = 19. The 3 + 10 + 6 pose split also sums to 19 only if the hold is 6 poses, not the sim's 5.
findings.fix: Make the sim formula the single source. Rewrite the stage table, V4, the Game Feel row and the Gaps bullet to 'hold = the last floor(3 x n / 10) poses, 5 at n = 19 to 10 at n = 36 (25 to 50 ticks)', and re-split the shares to sum to n (for example 3 + 11 + 5 at n = 19). Add to AC-HE-117 or AC-HE-143 that the first reach_c pose tick equals hold_start_T.

findings.section: HE-25 / HE-19 / E-HE-29 / HE-F10 / AC-HE-48 (new gap exposed by adopting door_passage)
findings.finding: HE-25 builds the pathing graph 'from Layout room_adjacency(section_id) over every section of its body (sections_of)', and HE-F10 sizes the largest welded body at 14 rooms (5+4+5). E-HE-29 says the horror 'may path across the new join'. But room_adjacency is per section. A HATCH record's room_b is EXTERIOR (AC-114 'EXTERIOR for hull-adjacent rooms'). door_passage answers 'each section for its OWN leaf in its OWN frame'. No published Layout read names the mated room across a seam, so a room-hop count (`linked`, ingress 'one room hop from the seat's room') or a BFS edge between two sections of a welded body is undefined. The weld fixture of AC-HE-48 and E-HE-29's cross-join path cannot be implemented against published reads.
findings.fix: Under G6 (GAP) have Layout add a seam-mate read, for example `hatch_mate(section_id, via_id) -> {section_id, room_id, via_id}` or fill room_b with the mate room once welded. Horror's graph then adds an edge per mated hatch pair using the shared open_extent_px. Alternatively state that MVP pathing, linked and ingress are per-section and a weld only triggers the HE-22 re-base, and reduce HE-F10, E-HE-29 and AC-HE-48 to match.

findings.section: HE-26 door eject / HE-43 / AC-HE-104 / AC-HE-137 (carried over)
findings.finding: HE-26 says the eject uses 'at most four queries, inside the five-query budget'. HE-19 says the five solid_in queries per run 'already belong to movement' (one LocomotionStep per tick, five ticks). Nothing says the eject run skips its walk, so an eject run can use up to 9 queries. AC-HE-104 asserts 'solid_in queries <= 5' on 'any run', so a correct implementation of AC-HE-137 fails AC-HE-104.
findings.fix: State in HE-26 and guard 4 that an eject run performs the ejection instead of the run's walk (no LocomotionStep that run), so the run total stays at or below 5. Alternatively raise the cap to 9 for a run on which `horror_door_ejected` increments, in HE-43, AC-HE-104 and AC-HE-137.

findings.section: AC-HE-17, HE-11, HE-35, HE-42 (carried over)
findings.finding: AC-HE-17 says 'the next waypoint is the lowest `hash(entity_id, dwell_index, HE_HASH_SEED)`', which has no per-candidate term, so all candidates tie and the order is undefined. HE-11 and HE-42 use `he_hash(entity_id, dwell_index, anchor_local_key, SALT_WP)`. `run_n` (HE-35, HE-42, AC-HE-139) is still never defined; E-HE-47 only says 'the run index'. `anchor_local_key` is unique only within a section, but the candidates span sections of a body, so ties are possible.
findings.fix: Rewrite AC-HE-17: 'the lowest he_hash(entity_id, dwell_index, anchor_local_key, SALT_WP) among legal candidates, ties lowest (section_id, anchor_local_key); golden input he_hash(7, 3, 0, SALT_WP) = 0x42973A88C2EF0EA3'. Define `run_n = T div HORROR_RUN_TICKS` in HE-42. Qualify the key with `section_id` (or fold it into k3).

findings.section: AC-HE-106 and the Feel Acceptance checklist (untestable as written)

The rig has no facings (ART 5.6, the Visual/Audio animation table 'Facings: none'), and AC-HE-107 uses 8 aim directions, so 'five facings' has no definition and no tester can enumerate it. findings.section: HE-F9 / HE-20 / E-HE-33 / AC-HE-44 / AC-HE-125 (carried over, partly mitigated)
findings.finding: The three-knob relation still sums to exactly TELL_MIN_TICKS (300 + 240 + 60 = 600, 'no slack'). Attention enters BREACH on its 6-tick grid. Horror's arrival is 'min T with T mod 5 = 0', so for an unpinned 600-tick tell the fallback body registers up to 4 ticks after BREACH entry. HE-F9 admits 'up to 4 ticks later', yet AC-HE-44 requires `horror_ingress_pending` 'clear before BREACH entry' and fails a build that enters BREACH with ingress pending. The ACs pin the TELL entry to T mod 30 = 0 or 5, which hides the case.
findings.fix: Add the run-alignment margin to the relation: `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS + STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR_TICKS + INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS + (HORROR_RUN_TICKS - 1) <= TELL_MIN_TICKS`, and lower the default STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR_TICKS to 230 (590 + 4 <= 600). Alternatively state in AC-HE-44 that pending must clear 'by the first Horror run at or after BREACH entry'. Add an unpinned-entry fixture (TELL entry at T mod 30 = 6, 12, 18, 24).

findings.section: AC-HE-133, E-HE-56, AC-HE-94 (decompression figure)
findings.finding: The pass line is 'about 131 s = 7860 ticks at the initial hole, LSG:707, a figure to be re-cited on the confirming run'. In life-support-graph.md the BREACH-EVENT row is now at line 775 and reads '131 s at the initial hole; with the stressed fatigue growing it, 105-120 s'. A RUPTURE only follows a GOUGE (a fatigued segment) during a BREACH (a stressed section), so the relevant clock is 105 s (6300 ticks), not 131 s. The 'to be re-cited' marker is still pending after this pass.
findings.fix: Re-cite by name (Life-Support Graph D.15 BREACH-EVENT) and use 105 s = 6300 ticks as the walk-and-close deadline in AC-HE-133 (131 s only as the initial-hole value). Remove 'to be re-cited on the confirming run'. Keep the rule that the assertion reads the Graph's published failures().

findings.section: Tuning Knobs HORROR_MARK_DRAW_GROUPS, AC-HE-100, C-HE-31
findings.finding: The knob default is 4 with a load assertion `<= D_marks - TRAIL_DMARKS_SHARE`, which needs D_marks >= 10. The Pipeline range is D_marks 4..20 with no registered default (its spike example uses 10). For D_marks 4..9 the assertion fails the load of the type row, so the build refuses to boot the horror over an open draw-budget question (C-HE-31), while the knob text says Horror 'gets none'. Those are two different outcomes (boot failure versus no marks). Under R21 the open item should be decided.
findings.fix: Decide C-HE-31 now: effective groups = max(0, min(knob, D_marks - TRAIL_DMARKS_SHARE)) with a diagnostic, and adopt the proposed floor 'the newest HAIRLINES/STRUCK mark of the current epoch is always drawn' (least new content, keeps the truth channel). Then AC-HE-100 can assert it instead of reading NOT ASSESSED.

The file is 512,619 bytes (1774 lines, 145 ACs). review-receipts.sh printed RECEIPT, CHANGED for the GDD and CHANGED for the registry; both changed since the last logged review, as expected after the 2026-10-28 cross-GDD fix pass. gdd-structure-check.sh reports PRESENT for all 8 required sections: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria. Every GDD named in Dependencies exists. Only Depth Rings & Scarcity, Knowledge Codex & Logs and Co-op have no file, and under R9 they stay provisional. Both prior blockers are RESOLVED, checked in this file and in Layout. (1) door_passage: Layout now publishes it (LY-28, D.5, AC-180) and HE-19/25 and AC-127/128 conform to its fields, formula and foot extents. (2) AC-HE-88 vs AC-HE-130: both now use HE-F5's convention, and I recomputed the a = 54 and a = 59 cases. I also recomputed the other numbers I spot-checked, and they hold. These were the Poisson table, the 324-pair enumeration, the 7-of-18 carrier figure, the mark-ring arithmetic, the L3 flash rate, the integrity ladder and bounds, the REACH timeline and the golden UNFOLD_TICKS lists. The recommended items fall into four groups. Cross-GDD naming and ownership: `threat_counter` exists only in this GDD while the kernel exports `rng_derive_epoch`, which also leaves AC-HE-136's NOT ASSESSED sentence stale; and the UNFOLD_SCALE_PCT command is specified with a HOST origin the kernel does not have. Unresolved carry-overs: the hold stage is defined two ways (25-50 ticks in the sim, 30-55 in the art and feel tables), the door-eject run can reach 9 solid_in queries against a cap of 5, AC-HE-17's hash is stale, the ingress fallback has no slack for the 5/6-tick grid, and a stale-text sweep is still owed. A gap the new door_passage exposed: no read pairs hatches across a welded seam, so welded-body pathing is undefined. Open items that R21 says should be decided: the Rime palette entry, the D_marks floor and the Suit patch-cap range floor. The registry's horror.state manifest is stale against HE-41. None of these makes implementation of slice 1 wrong or impossible, but items 1 and 2 should land before slice 1 starts because they gate it.
